````text
# Spec: `core-platform`

Status: Approved by project owner on 2026-09-24  
Capability: `core-platform`  
Capability Map: [`CAPABILITY-MAP.md`](./CAPABILITY-MAP.md)  
Cross-module product requirements: [`PRODUCT-REQUIREMENTS.md`](./PRODUCT-REQUIREMENTS.md)<br>
Last updated: 2026-09-26

## 1. Objective

Establish the shared technical foundation for the single-restaurant wedding management system before any business module is implemented. This capability must make four independent repositories buildable, testable, contract-compatible, secure by default, and ready for later modules:

| Repository | Runtime responsibility |
|---|---|
| `wedding-be` | Express REST API, all authoritative business rules, PostgreSQL access, integrations, audit records, and API contract generation |
| `wedding-web` | Next.js public website, Guest invitation/RSVP flows, and Couple Web flows |
| `wedding-manage-web` | Next.js Manager and Staff administration flows |
| `wedding-app` | Expo/React Native Android app for Couple workflows |

The backend is the only authority for validation that affects business state, authorization, booking, payment, refund, invitation delivery, seating, or check-in. Clients may validate for user experience, but must never replace server-side validation or derive their own business rules.

`core-platform` is complete when all four repositories share one API contract, have reproducible toolchains and quality gates, and the backend provides the infrastructure primitives required by every later capability.

## 2. Locked Assumptions

These assumptions are part of this draft and should be corrected before approval if any is wrong.

1. The product serves exactly one restaurant. No `tenantId`, tenant routing, tenant database policy, or tenant-specific configuration is introduced.
2. The repositories remain independent Git repositories; they are not converted into a monorepo and do not share a local npm workspace.
3. All clients call `wedding-be` over versioned JSON REST endpoints. Next.js does not own duplicate business APIs or access PostgreSQL directly.
4. PostgreSQL and Storage are hosted by Supabase, but Supabase Auth and direct client-side database access are not used.
5. API-driven updates use polling every 3–5 seconds only where a later module needs near-real-time data. Supabase Realtime is not part of the required architecture.
6. The system stores instants in UTC and applies `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` when interpreting restaurant dates, shifts, deadlines, and displays.
7. Currency is VND. API money fields are integer VND amounts; the database uses `Decimal(18,0)`. Floating-point money calculations are forbidden.
8. UUID strings identify persisted resources. API timestamps use ISO 8601/RFC 3339 strings with an explicit offset, normally UTC `Z`.
9. The first demo deployment may run one backend process. Scaling beyond one process requires a shared rate-limit store and operational review first.
10. UI language, design system, and detailed screen behavior belong to the relevant product-module specs, not this platform spec.

## 3. Scope

### 3.1 Required

- Scaffold and configure all four TypeScript repositories with npm and committed `package-lock.json` files.
- Establish repository responsibilities and dependency direction.
- Provide the Express application lifecycle, configuration loader, graceful shutdown, health/readiness endpoints, and a standard middleware pipeline.
- Configure Prisma ORM and Prisma Migrate for Supabase PostgreSQL.
- Define stable HTTP, validation, error, pagination, date, money, identifier, and idempotency conventions.
- Generate and commit an OpenAPI 3.1 contract from backend Zod schemas.
- Generate typed client schemas in all three client repositories from the committed backend OpenAPI artifact.
- Define provider boundaries and initial adapters for Supabase Storage, Resend, and AI image generation.
- Provide structured logging, request correlation, audit-log infrastructure, baseline RED metrics, and optional OpenTelemetry export.
- Establish secure defaults for CORS, headers, secrets, external calls, uploads, dependency installation, and error disclosure.
- Establish unit, integration, contract, and client smoke-test conventions.
- Configure the Expo project for Android-first development and a later EAS preview build.

### 3.2 Explicitly out of scope

- Accounts, JWT issuance, refresh rotation, password hashing, RBAC policy, and account activation; these belong to `identity-access`.
- Restaurant, hall, shift, menu, booking, payment, invitation, RSVP, seating, staff, notification, and dashboard business behavior.
- VNPay routes or callbacks.
- Email templates and scheduled email/push workflows.
- AI prompt design, invitation editing, or selection of a fixed Gemini model identifier; those belong to `invitation-studio`.
- Production deployment-provider selection, DNS setup, monitoring vendor selection, and the final Android EAS artifact; those are finalized in `release-demo`.
- iOS acceptance, guest mobile application, multi-tenant behavior, and automatic VNPay refunds.

## 4. Architecture and Dependency Rules

```text
┌──────────────────────┐     ┌──────────────────────┐
│ wedding-web          │     │ wedding-manage-web   │
│ Public/Guest/Couple  │     │ Manager/Staff        │
└──────────┬───────────┘     └──────────┬───────────┘
           │ HTTPS REST + generated API types       │
           └─────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                             │
                    ┌────────▼────────┐
                    │ wedding-be      │
                    │ Express API     │
                    └───────┬─────────┘
                            │ Prisma / provider adapters
          ┌─────────────────┼──────────────────┐
          │                 │                  │
   Supabase Postgres  Supabase Storage       Resend
                                              │
                                      Gemini via provider

                  wedding-app
          Expo Android ──HTTPS REST──────────► wedding-be
```

Rules:

- A client repository may depend on the API contract, never on backend source files.
- `wedding-be` must not import files from any client repository.
- A domain module may depend only on `src/core`, its declared provider contracts, and modules listed as dependencies in the Capability Map.
- Cross-module calls use a provider-owned application interface or a persisted domain event. Importing another module's repository implementation is forbidden.
- Integration SDK objects must not escape `src/integrations`; domain and application services depend on local interfaces.
- No repository may contain a second implementation of booking, payment, authorization, refund, or check-in rules.

## 5. Technology Baseline

The exact resolved dependency graph is committed in each repository's `package-lock.json`. Stable patches may be upgraded after tests pass; major upgrades require a spec change and project-owner approval.

| Area | Baseline | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime | Node.js `24.21.0` LTS | Pin in `.nvmrc`/`.node-version`; `engines.node` is `>=24.11 <25` |
| Package manager | npm 11.x | One `package-lock.json` per repository; no pnpm/yarn lockfiles |
| Language | TypeScript `5.9.3` | Deliberate compatibility pin across Prisma 7 and Expo 57; strict mode everywhere |
| Public and management web | Next.js `16.3.6`, React/React DOM `19.2.3` | App Router, TypeScript, stable releases only |
| API | Express `5.2.1` | ESM TypeScript service on Node 24 |
| ORM | Prisma CLI and Client `7.10.0`, `@prisma/adapter-pg` `7.10.0` | Prisma 8 is not used while it is a release candidate |
| Mobile | Expo SDK 57, React Native `0.86`, React `19.2.3` | Managed/CNG project, Expo Router, Android acceptance target |
| Android cloud build | EAS CLI `23.2.0` | Pin the CLI used by the project; preview build only until `release-demo` |
| Boundary validation | Zod `4.6.5` | HTTP, environment, and third-party responses |
| API description | OpenAPI `3.1.0`, `zod-openapi` `6.0.2` | Zod route schemas generate the canonical artifact |
| Client API access | `openapi-typescript` + `openapi-fetch` stable compatible releases | Exact versions locked at scaffold time |
| Unit/integration tests | Vitest 5.x | Backend and both Next.js repositories |
| Expo tests | Jest with SDK-57-compatible `jest-expo` | Installed with `npx expo install` when applicable |
| Web end-to-end tests | Playwright stable | Full flows are added by product modules |
| Linting/formatting | ESLint `10.11.x` flat config, Prettier 3.x | No legacy `.eslintrc` |
| Logging | Pino + `pino-http` | Structured JSON in production, readable transport in local development |
| Metrics/tracing | `prom-client`; OpenTelemetry Node SDK when configured | Vendor-neutral telemetry; no required paid vendor |

Version rules:

- Do not use `latest`, `next`, `beta`, `rc`, `canary`, or preview tags in committed manifests.
- Expo-managed packages are installed with `npx expo install`, not manually versioned with `npm install`.
- `prisma` and `@prisma/client` stay on the same 7.x release line.
- A security patch may supersede the patch above before implementation; if so, use the newest stable security patch in the same major/minor line and record it in this file.

## 6. Commands

The following scripts are required outcomes of implementing this spec. They need not exist before implementation begins.

### 6.1 Every repository

```bash
npm ci
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm run test
npm run test:coverage
npm run build
npm audit
```

CI uses `npm ci`, never `npm install`, and fails if the lockfile is inconsistent. New dependencies are first installed with lifecycle scripts disabled for review; required scripts are then explicitly allowed and a clean install is verified.

### 6.2 `wedding-be`

```bash
npm run dev
npm run build
npm run start
npm run test:unit
npm run test:integration
npm run test:contract
npm run db:generate
npm run db:migrate -- --name <migration_name>
npm run db:migrate:deploy
npm run db:seed
npm run db:studio
npm run api:generate
npm run api:check
```

### 6.3 `wedding-web` and `wedding-manage-web`

```bash
npm run dev
npm run build
npm run start
npm run test:unit
npm run test:e2e
npm run api:generate
npm run api:check
```

### 6.4 `wedding-app`

```bash
npx expo start
npx expo start --android
npx expo-doctor
npm run build
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm run test
npm run api:generate
npm run api:check
npx eas-cli@23.2.0 build -p android --profile preview
```

The EAS command is a release verification target, not a required cloud build during `core-platform`; `release-demo` owns the final downloadable Android artifact. EAS services have usage limits and may incur cost.

## 8. Configuration and Environments

Environments are `development`, `test`, `staging`, and `production`. Every repository commits `.env.example` with placeholders and gitignores all real `.env*` files except examples.

### 8.1 Backend configuration

Required or reserved variables:

```text
NODE_ENV
PORT
LOG_LEVEL
RESTAURANT_TIME_ZONE=Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
DATABASE_URL
MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL
SUPABASE_URL
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
SUPABASE_STORAGE_BUCKET
RESEND_API_KEY
RESEND_FROM_EMAIL
BREVO_API_KEY
BREVO_FROM_EMAIL
AI_IMAGE_PROVIDER=gemini
GEMINI_API_KEY
GEMINI_IMAGE_MODEL
METRICS_ENABLED
METRICS_TOKEN
OPENAPI_ENABLED=false
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
```

Rules:

- Zod validates environment variables once at process startup. Invalid or missing required production configuration terminates the process before the HTTP port opens.
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, Brevo, Resend, database, metrics, and Gemini secrets exist only in backend environments.
- Configure one complete email credential group (`BREVO_*` or legacy `RESEND_*`); staging/production requires email, and simultaneous providers are rejected.
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` and model are optional while AI is disabled; enabling the Gemini adapter without them is a startup error.
- `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is an explicit comma-separated allowlist for the two web deployments. Wildcard origins are forbidden when credentials are accepted.
- The committed OpenAPI artifact is served outside production. Production serving requires `OPENAPI_ENABLED=true`.
- Frontend variables prefixed `NEXT_PUBLIC_` or `EXPO_PUBLIC_` are public by definition and must never contain a secret.

### 8.2 Client configuration

```text
# Both Next.js repositories
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL

# Expo repository
EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL
EXPO_PUBLIC_EAS_PROJECT_ID
```

The production API base URL must be HTTPS. A development-only cleartext URL may be used for a local Android emulator with explicit platform configuration.

## 9. Database and Migration Contract

- Only `wedding-be` owns the database schema and migrations.
- Use a dedicated PostgreSQL role for Prisma rather than the Supabase dashboard's broad default role.
- For a persistent backend, `DATABASE_URL` uses a direct connection when IPv6 is available or Supavisor session mode on port 5432 when it is not.
- `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL` uses a direct connection when available; session mode is the fallback. Transaction-pooler mode must never run Prisma Migrate.
- TLS is required for database connections.
- `prisma.config.ts` reads `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL`; the runtime pool uses `DATABASE_URL` through `@prisma/adapter-pg`.
- Development schema changes use `prisma migrate dev`. Staging and production use `prisma migrate deploy` as an explicit release step.
- `prisma db push` is prohibited for shared, staging, demo, and production databases.
- Applied migration files are immutable. Corrections are new forward migrations; history is not rewritten after sharing.
- Destructive migrations require a written expand/migrate/contract plan, backup/restore evidence, and project-owner approval.
- Integration tests run against PostgreSQL, not SQLite, so constraints, transactions, indexes, and concurrency behavior match production.

### 9.1 Core-owned models

`core-platform` owns only infrastructure records. Domain tables are introduced by later module specs.

**`AuditLog`**

- `id`, `occurredAt`, `requestId`
- `actorType`: `SYSTEM`, `USER`, or `GUEST_LINK`
- nullable opaque `actorId`; no dependency on the future identity table
- stable `action`, `entityType`, nullable `entityId`
- redacted JSON `metadata`
- append-only through application code; no update/delete repository methods

Audit metadata must not contain passwords, JWTs, refresh tokens, guest invitation tokens, payment secrets, raw email bodies, or unnecessary PII.

**`IdempotencyRecord`**

- `id`, `namespace`, `idempotencyKey`, `requestHash`
- `status`: `IN_PROGRESS`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`
- nullable `responseStatus`, redacted `responseBody`, `resourceType`, and `resourceId`
- `lockedAt`, `expiresAt`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`
- unique constraint on `(namespace, idempotencyKey)`

## 10. REST API Contract

### 10.1 General conventions

- Base path: `/api/v1`.
- Resource paths use plural nouns and kebab-case only when a compound noun is unavoidable.
- JSON field names and query parameters use `camelCase`.
- Enum values use `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`.
- Request/response `Content-Type` is `application/json`, except explicit file transfers.
- `POST` creates a resource or initiates a named operation that cannot be modeled as CRUD; `PATCH` applies partial updates; `DELETE` is idempotent where supported.
- New response fields are additive and optional to old clients. Removing or changing an existing field requires a new API major version.
- Clients branch on machine-readable codes and fields, never on human message text.

Single-resource success:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "8c195f40-0d10-44c5-a344-1705652ce3dd",
    "createdAt": "2026-09-24T08:30:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

Paginated collection success:

```json
{
  "data": [],
  "pagination": {
    "page": 1,
    "pageSize": 20,
    "totalItems": 0,
    "totalPages": 0
  }
}
```

List endpoints default to `page=1&pageSize=20`, cap `pageSize` at 100, document a deterministic default sort, and add `id` as a final tie-breaker.

### 10.2 Error contract

Every non-2xx application response uses:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
    "message": "The request is invalid.",
    "details": [
      {
        "path": "email",
        "code": "invalid_format",
        "message": "Email must be valid."
      }
    ],
    "requestId": "24dcfaac-4408-4d42-8d66-456ed6ee7ea4"
  }
}
```

Status mapping:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `400` | Malformed syntax or unsupported request shape |
| `401` | Missing or invalid authentication |
| `403` | Authenticated actor lacks permission |
| `404` | Resource is absent or intentionally concealed |
| `409` | State/version conflict or duplicate request still in progress |
| `422` | Syntactically valid request fails schema or business validation |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded; include `Retry-After` |
| `500` | Unexpected internal error with generic public message |
| `502`/`503`/`504` | Explicit upstream failure/unavailability/timeout |

Stack traces, SQL messages, provider payloads, and secret-bearing details never appear in public responses.

### 10.3 Health and internal endpoints

- `GET /health/live`: process liveness only; no dependency calls.
- `GET /health/ready`: bounded PostgreSQL readiness check and configuration status; returns `503` when not ready.
- `GET /api/v1/openapi.json`: serves the exact committed OpenAPI artifact outside production, and may be explicitly enabled in production.
- `GET /internal/metrics`: disabled unless configured; when enabled, protected by network policy or a dedicated bearer secret and excluded from public OpenAPI documentation.

### 10.4 Idempotency

Later module specs mark which state-changing routes require `Idempotency-Key`. At minimum, booking creation, payment creation/recording, refund recording, and notification dispatch must use it.

- Key length is 1–128 printable ASCII characters and identifies one user intent, not one retry attempt.
- Namespace includes actor scope, HTTP method, normalized route, and operation version.
- Actor scope comes only from authenticated or otherwise trusted request context, never from a client-controlled header, query, or body field.
- A missing required header returns `400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`; a malformed key returns `422 INVALID_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY`.
- Before the side effect, atomically insert an `IN_PROGRESS` record; the database unique constraint chooses the winner.
- Store a SHA-256 hash of the canonical request payload. Reusing a key with a different payload returns `422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.
- A concurrent duplicate receives `409 REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS` with `Retry-After`; it never executes the side effect.
- A completed duplicate receives the stored status/body or the canonical resource reference.
- Successful `2xx` responses become `SUCCEEDED`; deterministic `4xx` responses become `FAILED` and are replayable. `3xx` and `5xx` responses remain `IN_PROGRESS` because their side-effect outcome is not proven.
- Default retention is 30 days. Payment operations retain records for at least 180 days or longer if the provider's retry/dispute path requires it.
- A timeout after calling an external provider is an unknown outcome, not an automatic failure. Keep enough state for reconciliation before any retry.

## 11. API Contract Distribution Across Four Repositories

Zod schemas in `wedding-be` are the runtime validation source and the source for generated OpenAPI 3.1.

1. `npm run api:generate` in `wedding-be` deterministically produces `openapi/openapi.json`.
2. `npm run api:check` regenerates to a temporary file and fails when the committed artifact differs.
3. Each client repository runs `openapi-typescript` against `OPENAPI_SOURCE`, which defaults locally to `../wedding-be/openapi/openapi.json`, and writes only `src/lib/api/generated/schema.d.ts`.
4. Generated files are committed with a header containing the OpenAPI SHA-256 digest and must never be hand-edited.
5. Each client wraps `openapi-fetch` once in `src/lib/api/client.ts` to set the base URL, authorization strategy, timeout, request ID, and normalized error handling.
6. Client CI receives an artifact from an exact backend commit/release, never a moving branch URL, verifies its digest, and then runs `api:check`.
7. A backend contract change is merged first. Coordinated client pull requests regenerate from the new artifact before using new fields or paths.
8. Contract tests verify that documented examples and actual health/error responses satisfy the artifact.

This avoids a fifth shared-code repository while preserving a single contract authority.

## 12. Provider Boundaries

Provider contracts live in backend-owned application interfaces. Adapters translate and validate external SDK inputs/outputs.

```ts
export interface EmailProvider {
  send(command: SendEmailCommand): Promise<SentEmail>;
}

export interface StorageProvider {
  put(command: PutObjectCommand): Promise<StoredObject>;
  createSignedReadUrl(objectKey: string, expiresInSeconds: number): Promise<string>;
  delete(objectKey: string): Promise<void>;
}

export interface AiImageProvider {
  generate(command: GenerateImageCommand): Promise<GeneratedImage[]>;
}
```

Conventions demonstrated by the snippet:

- Type/interface names use `PascalCase`; variables and functions use `camelCase`; files use `kebab-case`.
- Commands and return values are explicit types rather than raw SDK payloads.
- No `any`; external `unknown` values are parsed with Zod before use.
- Interfaces describe business-needed capability, not every feature of the vendor SDK.

### 12.1 Supabase Storage

- Backend service credentials are the only privileged Storage credentials.
- Start with separate private buckets by security class rather than one public catch-all bucket. The initial required bucket is `wedding-private`.
- Object keys are server-generated and scoped by purpose/resource UUID; user-provided filenames never become filesystem/object paths.
- Reads use short-lived signed URLs, default 15 minutes. Never persist signed URLs; persist object keys.
- Upload policy allowlists MIME types and extensions, caps byte size, verifies actual content/magic bytes where applicable, and records checksum/size.
- A successful upload is not trusted until the backend finalizes and validates it.
- Deletion requires the caller's resource authorization and an allowlisted key prefix; never accept an arbitrary bucket or path from the client.

### 12.2 Transactional email

- `EmailProvider` supports `BrevoEmailProvider`, the retained `ResendEmailProvider`, and an offline fake. Brevo is the recommended project configuration; setup is documented in `docs/brevo-email.md`.
- Brevo requires an API key and a verified sender configured through `BREVO_FROM_EMAIL`. Brevo temporarily rewrites free sender addresses; an authenticated domain is recommended for long-term delivery. Legacy Resend production/staging uses a verified sending domain and configured `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL`.
- Every retryable email intent uses a deterministic provider idempotency key derived from event type and persisted event/entity ID.
- Provider key retention does not replace the application's durable delivery/audit state. Brevo uses a deterministic UUID v5 and documents a 30-minute deduplication window; duplicate rejections are not successful response replays, and the adapter does not automatically retry.
- Provider timeouts and returned shapes are validated and normalized; raw provider errors remain in redacted server logs.

### 12.3 AI image generation

- The initial adapter target is Gemini, selected through `AI_IMAGE_PROVIDER=gemini`.
- `GEMINI_IMAGE_MODEL` remains configuration so the invitation module can choose a currently supported production model without changing domain code.
- Model prompts never include guest contact data, payment data, authentication data, or other unnecessary PII.
- Model output is untrusted: validate MIME type, dimensions, byte size, and response shape before storing or rendering it.
- The model cannot call tools, write database state, construct SQL, choose storage paths, or authorize an action.
- Provider quota, timeout, safety refusal, and invalid-output failures map to stable internal error codes.

## 13. Security Baseline

### 13.1 Trust boundaries and assets

Untrusted boundaries include public/guest HTTP input, authenticated client input, file uploads, provider callbacks, Resend/Supabase/Gemini responses, environment configuration, and AI output. Protected assets include credentials, user sessions, guest tokens, guest PII, booking state, payment state, audit evidence, and uploaded/generated files.

Required controls:

- Validate request params, query, headers, and bodies before application logic; reject unknown fields on write schemas unless explicitly allowed.
- Use Prisma parameterization. Raw SQL requires parameter binding, a written reason, and a focused test.
- Apply Helmet security headers and explicit CORS origins. Next.js repositories define restrictive CSPs when their external asset requirements are known.
- Bound JSON body size and request duration. Upload endpoints use separate, stricter limits.
- Apply a general rate limit and stricter limits to future authentication, guest-token, payment, and file endpoints.
- The in-memory limiter is permitted only while one backend process is deployed. Horizontal scaling is blocked until a shared limiter store exists.
- Configure outbound provider calls with HTTPS, allowlisted fixed hosts, connect/response timeouts, and bounded retries with jitter.
- Do not fetch arbitrary user-provided URLs. A future requirement to do so needs an SSRF design review.
- Never log request/response bodies by default. Redact `authorization`, cookies, tokens, secrets, email, phone, and payment fields.
- Never store authentication tokens in browser `localStorage`. The exact web-cookie/mobile-secure-store flow is defined in `identity-access`.
- Commit placeholders only. If a secret reaches Git or logs, rotate it before history cleanup.
- Release gates include lockfile-based dependency audit; critical/high findings must be fixed or documented with reachability, mitigation, owner, and review date.

### 13.2 Data minimization and retention

- Every later schema field containing PII must state its purpose and retention rule in that module's spec.
- Logs and metrics contain no names, phone numbers, email addresses, invitation tokens, or message bodies.
- Audit metadata is allowlisted rather than copied from request bodies.
- Backup, export, correction, and deletion behavior is finalized before production launch; a soft-delete flag alone is not treated as erasure.

## 14. Observability and Auditability

Questions the platform must answer without reading source code:

1. Is the API alive and able to reach PostgreSQL?
2. Which request failed, on which normalized route, and because of which stable error/provider code?
3. Are endpoint or provider error rates and p95/p99 latency degrading?
4. Which actor changed a protected business record, and under which request ID?

### 14.1 Application logs

- Production logs are newline-delimited JSON with stable `event` names.
- Every request has a UUID `requestId`; accept only a valid UUID from a trusted upstream, otherwise generate one, return it as `x-request-id`, and propagate it to providers.
- Common fields: `timestamp`, `level`, `service`, `environment`, `event`, `requestId`, `entryPoint`, `module`, `route`, `method`, `statusClass`, `durationMs`, and stable error/provider codes.
- Entry points are explicit: `http`, `scheduler`, `provider_callback`, `replay`, or `cli`.
- `debug` is disabled in production. `error` means action may be required; handled degradation is `warn`; material business events are `info`.

### 14.2 Metrics and tracing

- RED metrics cover HTTP routes and external providers: request count, error count, and duration histogram.
- Metric labels are bounded values such as route template, method, status class, module, and provider. IDs, raw URLs, emails, error messages, and request IDs are forbidden labels.
- Histograms support p50, p95, and p99; averages are not the only latency signal.
- OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation and OTLP export activate only when an endpoint is configured. The application runs correctly with tracing disabled.
- Product-module specs add business metrics only when they answer a named operational question.

### 14.3 Audit log versus diagnostic log

Audit logs are durable business/security evidence stored in PostgreSQL. Application logs are operational telemetry and may expire. A protected state change is not considered auditable merely because it produced a Pino log line.

## 15. Code Style

- TypeScript `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` are enabled where framework tooling permits.
- Use ESM, named exports for reusable code, and dependency injection at module composition boundaries.
- Route handlers translate HTTP to typed application commands; they do not contain Prisma or vendor SDK calls.
- Services express use cases; repositories persist; provider adapters translate external APIs.
- Prefer immutable values and small pure functions. Do not use non-null assertions to silence unresolved states.
- Use discriminated unions for state variants and branded/opaque types for IDs at domain boundaries where they prevent accidental substitution.
- Comments explain constraints or reasons, not a restatement of code.
- Prettier owns formatting; ESLint owns correctness/import rules. Formatting debates are not settled manually in reviews.

## 16. Testing Strategy

| Level | Purpose | Required evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Unit | Pure errors, serializers, money/time helpers, request hashing, provider mapping | Fast colocated tests; no network |
| Backend integration | Express middleware, Prisma repositories, migrations, transactions, concurrency | Disposable PostgreSQL; Supertest against the app without opening a real port |
| Contract | OpenAPI determinism, examples, common responses, generated client compatibility | `api:check` plus schema/response validation |
| Client unit/component | API wrapper, config, loading/error states, shared components | Vitest/Testing Library on web; Jest/jest-expo on app |
| Web E2E | Cross-repository user journeys | Playwright, added by the module owning the journey |
| Android verification | Native configuration and final demo behavior | `expo-doctor` now; physical/emulator checks and EAS artifact in `release-demo` |

Coverage gates for `core-platform`:

- At least 80% line and branch coverage for newly added core backend files.
- 100% branch coverage for environment validation, error mapping, idempotency claim/replay behavior, and secret-redaction helpers.
- Coverage numbers do not replace required concurrency, migration, contract, and failure-path tests.

Mandatory scenarios:

- Startup refuses invalid environment configuration.
- `health/live` remains independent of PostgreSQL; `health/ready` changes to `503` when PostgreSQL is unavailable.
- All validation failures use the standard error body and request ID.
- Concurrent use of one idempotency key produces one winning execution.
- Reusing a key with a different payload fails with `422`.
- OpenAPI generation is deterministic and all three clients regenerate without a diff.
- Provider adapters normalize timeout, refusal, invalid payload, and transient failure without exposing raw errors.
- Logs and audit metadata pass redaction tests.
- Clean migrations apply successfully to an empty PostgreSQL database.

## 17. Boundaries

### Always do

- Update this spec before changing a locked platform decision.
- Validate every external boundary and third-party response.
- Keep authoritative rules and database access in `wedding-be`.
- Commit migration files, OpenAPI output, generated client schema, and npm lockfiles.
- Add request correlation and meaningful structured telemetry with each new endpoint/provider/job.
- Add audit records for later-module actions that affect authorization, booking, money, guest access, seating, or attendance.
- Run lint, typecheck, relevant tests, build, contract check, and dependency audit before merge.
- Use stable/LTS dependencies and review new dependency ownership, install scripts, and lockfile changes.

### Ask the project owner first

- Add or replace a framework, database, ORM, package manager, auth mechanism, external provider, or repository.
- Add a new category of PII or send PII to a third party, including an AI provider.
- Change CORS, token transport, rate limits, upload policy, retention periods, or audit semantics.
- Make a breaking API change or create `/api/v2`.
- Run a destructive database migration or edit already-applied migration history.
- Make a storage bucket public or expose direct client database access.
- Introduce Redis, a queue, Supabase Realtime, or another paid infrastructure dependency.
- Enable iOS as an acceptance target.

### Never do

- Commit secrets, production data, service-role keys, signing keys, or real `.env` files.
- Put business logic, Prisma, or privileged Supabase access in a Next.js or Expo client.
- Use `prisma db push` against a shared environment.
- Trust client validation, filenames, MIME declarations, callbacks, provider responses, or AI output.
- Concatenate input into SQL, object paths, HTML, shell commands, or log messages.
- Log passwords, tokens, cookies, guest invitation links, full PII, payment secrets, or whole request bodies.
- Store browser auth tokens in `localStorage`, disable security headers for convenience, or use wildcard credentialed CORS.
- Hand-edit generated OpenAPI client files or ignore a contract diff.
- Delete/skip a failing test merely to make a pipeline pass.

## 18. Success Criteria

`core-platform` is accepted only when all of the following are demonstrated:

1. `CAPABILITY-MAP.md` names and correctly separates all four repositories without changing approved module IDs or build order.
2. All four repositories pin the approved runtime/framework baseline, contain exactly one npm lockfile, and pass clean `npm ci`.
3. Lint, typecheck, unit tests, coverage checks, and production builds pass in every repository.
4. `wedding-be` starts and shuts down gracefully; liveness/readiness behavior passes integration tests.
5. Prisma migrations apply to an empty PostgreSQL database and the application connects to Supabase-compatible PostgreSQL using the documented connection mode.
6. Common error, validation, pagination, time, money, identifier, and request-ID contracts are implemented and covered by tests.
7. Idempotency storage and middleware pass concurrent-winner, replay, payload-mismatch, and in-flight-duplicate tests.
8. OpenAPI 3.1 generation is deterministic, the artifact is committed, and all three clients generate matching typed schemas without hand edits.
9. Supabase Storage, Resend, and Gemini are reachable only through provider interfaces; fake adapters allow tests without paid/network calls.
10. Structured logs, audit primitives, RED metrics, redaction, and optional tracing behave as specified under induced success and failure cases.
11. `.env.example` documents every setting, real secrets are ignored, and no critical/high reachable production dependency finding remains unmitigated.
12. `wedding-app` uses the approved Expo structure, passes `expo-doctor`, and has an Android `preview` EAS profile ready for the later release module.

Approval of this spec authorizes Phase 2 planning for `core-platform`; it does not authorize implementation of later capability modules.

These inputs do not change the architecture and may remain placeholders during local implementation, but must be resolved before the named gate:

| Input | Needed by |

| Production/staging backend and Next.js hosting providers | `release-demo` deployment plan |
| Supabase project references, database credentials, and bucket names | Integration/staging setup |
| Resend verified domain and sender address | First real email test |

| Telemetry backend, if any | Production launch; local metrics/logging do not depend on it |
````

````text
# Specification: Identity and Access

Status: **Approved by project owner on 2026-10-03**
Module ID: `identity-access`
Requirement ownership: ACC-002 through ACC-007
Depends on: `core-platform`
Consumers: `venue-catalog`, `booking-lifecycle`, `payments-billing`, `invitation-studio`, `guest-rsvp`, `seating-plan`, `staff-operations`, `notifications-automation`, `analytics-dashboard`

## 1. Objective

Deliver the authoritative account, authentication, session, role, restricted-workspace,
and Couple-access-promotion boundary for the single-restaurant system.

The module must let an invited prospective couple establish an authenticated Web
session without turning the invitation token into a permanent credential. Before a
successful deposit, that identity receives only consultation proposal and timeline
collaboration access. A successful deposit promotes the same account and consultation
access grant to full Couple access without copying the account or consultation data.

The same identity boundary authenticates Manager and Staff users for the Management
Web and full Couple users for Public Web and Android. All authorization remains
backend-enforced from current account, session, role, and resource state.

## 2. Requirement Trace

| Requirement | Owned outcome                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ACC-002     | An expiring, single-use workspace invitation bootstraps a real session; its raw token is never a durable bearer credential.                               |
| ACC-003     | A `RESTRICTED` consultation access grant permits proposal read and timeline collaboration only for its consultation.                                      |
| ACC-004     | Restricted prospects are denied media, invitation, guest, seating, print, and event-operation capabilities by the backend.                                |
| ACC-005     | A successful deposit promotes the existing consultation access grant to `FULL` without creating another account or consultation.                          |
| ACC-006     | Expired, revoked, superseded, or consumed invitations cannot create another session; invitation revocation does not delete consultation or audit history. |
| ACC-007     | Authentication and authorization use current backend state; client route visibility is never an authorization boundary.                                   |

ACC-001 remains owned by `booking-lifecycle`. That module asks the identity provider
contract to issue or revoke a workspace invitation after it creates a consultation.
Payment truth remains outside this module; a successful payment path calls the
idempotent access-promotion contract.

## 3. Scope

### 3.1 Included

- Email/password accounts for Manager, Staff, Prospective Couple, and Couple actors.
- Password hashing, login, logout, password reset, and session inventory/revocation.
- Short-lived access credentials and rotating refresh credentials.
- Management roles and consultation-scoped Couple access grants.
- Workspace invitation issue, reissue, expiry, revocation, and atomic acceptance.
- Idempotent `RESTRICTED` to `FULL` promotion after a successful deposit.
- Backend authentication middleware and deny-by-default authorization helpers.
- OpenAPI contracts and generated clients for Web, Management Web, and Android.
- Minimal login, invitation acceptance, password reset, session restore, and logout UX.
- Durable audit events and redacted operational telemetry for security-sensitive actions.

### 3.2 Excluded

- Consultation creation, timeline data, booking state, or payment processing.
- Staff event assignment and staff operational permissions beyond base authentication.
- Staff account business provisioning; `staff-operations` owns that lifecycle and may
  call an identity-owned account/role port after its own specification is approved.
- Guest personalized-link authentication; Guests continue to use guest-link contracts.
- Social login, SSO, passkeys, MFA, phone/SMS login, or biometric identity.
- Multiple restaurants, organizations, or tenant switching.
- Production email templates, campaigns, reminders, and delivery automation beyond the
  identity notification port.
- Production domain, DNS, and final cross-site cookie configuration; `release-demo`
  validates those deployment inputs against the approved transport decision.

## 4. Inherited Decisions

- The backend is the only authorization authority.
- PostgreSQL/Prisma owns all durable identity state; clients never query it directly.
- Zod validates external boundaries and generates OpenAPI 3.1 contracts.
- Errors use the core `{ error: { code, message, details?, requestId } }` envelope.
- All identifiers are UUIDs, timestamps are UTC, and business-time presentation uses
  `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`.
- Real secrets live only in backend environment variables or approved device-secure
  storage. No auth token may enter logs, audit metadata, URLs, analytics, or browser
  `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`.
- The initial backend remains one replica. Horizontal scaling is blocked until auth
  rate limiting and other process-local controls use an approved shared store.
- Email delivery stays behind a local interface and is testable through fakes.

## 5. Approved Decisions

The project owner approved the following architecture decisions at Checkpoint H1 on
2026-10-03.

| ID  | Recommended decision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Reason / consequence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| D1  | First-party PostgreSQL auth with Node `crypto.scrypt`; random opaque access and refresh credentials stored only as hashes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Avoids a new auth provider and JWT key lifecycle; the single backend already needs a current-state database read for immediate revocation and ACC-007.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| D2  | Web keeps the short-lived access credential in memory and the rotating refresh credential in an `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, `__Host-` cookie with `Path=/` and no `Domain`. Android keeps only the refresh credential in Expo SecureStore and the access credential in memory.                                                                                                          | Prevents durable JavaScript-readable tokens while supporting Android. Unsafe cookie-authenticated requests also require an allowed `Origin`; `release-demo` must confirm the deployed Web/API hosts remain same-site.                                                                                                                  |
| D3  | Access lifetime 10 minutes; refresh idle lifetime 30 days; refresh absolute lifetime 90 days; password-reset lifetime 30 minutes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Limits stolen-token value while allowing practical session restoration. Refresh reuse revokes the whole session family.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| D4  | Workspace invitation lifetime 72 hours; only one active invitation per consultation/email; reissue atomically supersedes the prior token; at most 3 reissues per rolling 24 hours.                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Resolves the deferred invitation lifetime/reissue policy and bounds email/token abuse.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| D5  | Passwords are 12–128 characters with no composition rule; compare only through scrypt and constant-time equality. Separate fail-closed buckets apply per resolved client IP and normalized subject/token fingerprint: login and token consumption allow 10 attempts per 15 minutes, reset request allows 3 per hour, and refresh allows 60 per 15 minutes. There is no permanent account lockout. | Long passwords and layered throttling resist credential stuffing, distributed account targeting, token-endpoint abuse, and attacker-triggered permanent denial of service. Scrypt parameters must be benchmarked on the deployment runtime during IA-02; proxy-derived IPs are trusted only under an explicit deployment proxy policy. |
| D6  | Terminal invitation metadata is retained for 180 days; terminal password-reset metadata for 30 days; expired/revoked session metadata for 90 days. Disabled account PII is retained for 365 days after its last linked consultation/booking reaches a terminal state, then deleted or anonymized unless an active legal/financial hold applies.                                                   | Provides abuse/audit evidence while bounding identity PII. Raw credentials are never retained; backup purge timing remains a deployment-policy input for `release-demo`.                                                                                                                                                               |
| D7  | Accepting an invitation always requires a password. For a new account it sets the first credential; for an existing matching account it verifies the existing credential and never overwrites it.                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Preserves one identity per normalized email and prevents an invitation from silently resetting an existing password.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

Any change to D1, D2, D5, D6, roles, CORS, or rate limiting requires explicit
project-owner approval because it changes authentication, token transport, PII
retention, or security policy.

## 6. Architecture and Dependency Direction

```text
Public Web / Management Web / Android
                 |
                 | HTTPS + generated OpenAPI types
                 v
        identity-access HTTP boundary
                 |
        services + policy contracts
          /          |          \
 PostgreSQL      AuditService    IdentityNotificationPort
                                      |
                                  EmailProvider

booking-lifecycle ----> WorkspaceInvitationIssuer (owned here)
payments-billing  ----> CoupleAccessPromoter (owned here)
future modules    ----> AuthenticatedActor + ConsultationAccessReader
booking-lifecycle ----> AccountRetentionEligibilityRecorder (owned here)
```

Dependency arrows always point from later modules to `identity-access`. This module
stores opaque `consultationId`, `bookingId`, and `sourcePaymentId` UUID references but
does not import later modules or query their tables. Later migrations may add database
foreign keys after the owning tables exist without moving policy ownership.

## 7. Trust Boundaries and Threat Model

### 7.1 Assets

- Password verifiers, access/refresh credentials, invitation/reset credentials.
- Account email and profile identity.
- Manager/Staff roles and consultation access level.
- Active sessions, revocation state, and security audit evidence.
- The promotion boundary that unlocks post-deposit Couple capabilities.

### 7.2 Untrusted inputs

- Login, reset, invitation, and refresh requests.
- Cookie, authorization header, origin, IP/proxy metadata, and client-kind claims.
- Email links and Android deep links.
- Forwarded-IP headers and deployment proxy metadata.
- Calls from later module services to invitation and promotion ports.
- Email-provider responses and any delivery identifiers.

### 7.3 Required abuse cases

| Threat                  | Required behavior                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Credential stuffing     | Generic login errors, strict throttling, no account enumeration, audited failure aggregates without email/token logs.               |
| Stolen invitation       | High-entropy single-use token, short expiry, stored hash only, password requirement, atomic consume.                                |
| Reissue/accept race     | Exactly one of reissue or acceptance wins; a superseded token cannot create a session.                                              |
| Refresh replay          | One rotation wins; reuse revokes the session family and emits a security audit event.                                               |
| Session theft           | Short access lifetime, refresh rotation, immediate server-side revocation, no durable browser-readable credential.                  |
| IDOR / role forgery     | Every resource call uses the authenticated account plus consultation-scoped access read from PostgreSQL; request roles are ignored. |
| Premature Couple access | Only the promotion port can move `RESTRICTED` to `FULL`; clients cannot submit access level or payment state.                       |
| Account enumeration     | Login and reset request responses are indistinguishable for unknown, disabled, and known emails where practical.                    |
| Token leakage           | Tokens are prohibited from URL query strings, logs, metrics, audit metadata, response errors, and persisted plaintext.              |
| Privilege escalation    | Role assignment and access promotion are separate audited operations with allowlisted callers and no generic “set role” endpoint.   |

## 8. Domain Model

### 8.1 Account and roles

- `Account`: normalized unique email, display email, status, timestamps.
- `PasswordCredential`: one current scrypt verifier and parameter/version metadata.
- `AccountRole`: unique `(accountId, role)` where role is `MANAGER`, `STAFF`, or
  `COUPLE`. `PROSPECT` is not a global role; it is a consultation access level.
- A restricted prospect does not gain `COUPLE` solely by accepting an invitation.
  Promotion of any consultation to `FULL` atomically upserts the account's `COUPLE`
  role; the account keeps that role while another authorized business record may
  still require it.
- Account status is `ACTIVE`, `SUSPENDED`, or `DISABLED`. Only `ACTIVE` accounts may
  create or refresh sessions.
- A deployment/bootstrap procedure creates the first Manager. No public registration
  endpoint exists.

### 8.2 Consultation access

- `ConsultationAccess` uniquely links one account and consultation.
- Access level is `RESTRICTED` or `FULL`.
- `RESTRICTED` permits only consultation proposal read and timeline collaboration
  contracts supplied by `booking-lifecycle`.
- `FULL` is monotonic and records `promotedAt` and `sourcePaymentId`.
- Promotion never changes the account ID, email, password, session family, or
  consultation ID.

### 8.3 Invitations and sessions

- `WorkspaceInvitation` stores consultation, normalized recipient email, optional
  resolved account, issuer, sequence, token hash, status, expiry, and terminal times.
- `Session` stores account, client kind, status, refresh-family identity, idle and
  absolute expiry, last-seen time, and revocation reason.
- Access and refresh credential records contain hashes, expiries, status, and rotation
  linkage. The raw values exist only at issuance/transport boundaries.
- `PasswordResetCredential` stores only account, token hash, expiry, status, and
  terminal timestamps.

## 9. State Machines and Concurrency

### 9.1 Workspace invitation

```text
ACTIVE ──accept──> ACCEPTED
   ├────revoke──> REVOKED
   ├───reissue──> SUPERSEDED + new ACTIVE invitation
   └────expiry──> EXPIRED
```

- Accept is a conditional update from `ACTIVE` where `expiresAt > now`.
- A unique partial-equivalent policy is enforced transactionally so only one active
  invitation exists per consultation and normalized email.
- Acceptance atomically creates/reuses the account, verifies/sets the password,
  creates the `RESTRICTED` consultation access, consumes the invitation, and creates a
  Web session.
- Revocation and reissue never delete consultation or durable audit records.

### 9.2 Session and refresh rotation

```text
ACTIVE ──logout/admin revoke──> REVOKED
   ├────idle/absolute time────> EXPIRED
   └────refresh reuse─────────> COMPROMISED (family revoked)
```

- Access credential lookup requires an active account and session on every request.
- Refresh rotation atomically consumes the presented credential and creates its
  successor. Concurrent reuse cannot produce two successors.
- A consumed refresh credential presented again is treated as possible theft and
  revokes the family, including the winner's successor.
- Password reset completion revokes all sessions for the account.
- Retention eligibility is accepted only through the internal typed port, is audited,
  and never bypasses the 365-day wait or an active legal/financial hold.

### 9.3 Couple access promotion

```text
RESTRICTED ──successful-deposit evidence──> FULL
FULL ──duplicate promotion evidence───────> FULL (idempotent replay)
```

- The input contains account, consultation, and source payment identifiers; it never
  contains a caller-selected target level.
- A transaction/unique constraint chooses the winner under concurrent callbacks.
- A different account or consultation for an already-used payment identifier fails
  with conflict and emits an audit event.
- There is no demotion transition in this module. Refund/cancellation consequences
  must be specified by their owning future module before changing this rule.

## 10. Authorization Contract

Authentication produces this internal, immutable shape:

```typescript
type AuthenticatedActor = Readonly<{
  accountId: string;
  sessionId: string;
  roles: readonly ('MANAGER' | 'STAFF' | 'COUPLE')[];
}>;
```

The shape is created only from current database state. Handlers never accept account,
session, role, or access-level claims from a request body or query.

The provider API exposes:

```typescript
interface ConsultationAccessReader {
  requireAccess(
    input: Readonly<{
      accountId: string;
      consultationId: string;
      minimum: 'RESTRICTED' | 'FULL';
    }>,
  ): Promise<Readonly<{ level: 'RESTRICTED' | 'FULL' }>>;
}

interface WorkspaceInvitationIssuer {
  issue(input: IssueWorkspaceInvitationInput): Promise<IssuedWorkspaceInvitation>;
  reissue(input: ReissueWorkspaceInvitationInput): Promise<IssuedWorkspaceInvitation>;
  revoke(input: RevokeWorkspaceInvitationInput): Promise<void>;
}

interface CoupleAccessPromoter {
  promote(
    input: Readonly<{
      accountId: string;
      consultationId: string;
      sourcePaymentId: string;
    }>,
  ): Promise<Readonly<{ level: 'FULL'; replayed: boolean }>>;
}

interface AccountRetentionEligibilityRecorder {
  record(
    input: Readonly<{
      accountId: string;
      eligibleAfter: Date;
      sourceBusinessRecordId: string;
    }>,
  ): Promise<void>;
}
```

Later modules combine the actor and access reader with the current resource state that
they own. `identity-access` never calls `booking-lifecycle` or `payments-billing` to
discover that state, preventing a dependency cycle. Because identity does not own
consultation/booking terminality, the owning business module records an audited
retention-eligibility fact after every linked business record is terminal. Identity
requires a fact for every consultation access currently linked to the account, so a
new invitation/link automatically blocks erasure. Identity still enforces D6's waiting
period and legal/financial holds before erasure or anonymization.

## 11. Draft HTTP Contract

All routes live under `/api/v1`, use strict Zod schemas, the common error envelope,
`Cache-Control: no-store`, and the existing request ID. Secret-bearing inputs must not
be echoed.

| Method and path                          | Authentication                   | Contract summary                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `POST /auth/web-sessions`                | Public                           | Email/password login; returns short-lived access credential and account summary, sets rotating refresh cookie. |
| `POST /auth/android-sessions`            | Public                           | Email/password login; returns access and refresh credentials once.                                             |
| `POST /auth/web-session-refreshes`       | Refresh cookie + allowed Origin  | Atomically rotates refresh cookie and returns a new access credential.                                         |
| `POST /auth/android-session-refreshes`   | Refresh credential body          | Atomically rotates and returns both credentials.                                                               |
| `DELETE /auth/sessions/current`          | Access credential                | Revokes the current session and clears a Web refresh cookie when present.                                      |
| `GET /auth/me`                           | Access credential                | Returns current account ID, roles, session ID, and safe profile fields; no credential or password metadata.    |
| `POST /auth/password-reset-requests`     | Public                           | Always returns the same accepted response; sends a reset intent only for eligible accounts.                    |
| `POST /auth/password-reset-completions`  | Reset credential in POST body    | Atomically consumes the credential, changes the password, and revokes all sessions.                            |
| `POST /workspace-invitation-acceptances` | Invitation credential + password | Atomically accepts an invitation and creates a restricted Web session.                                         |
| `GET /auth/sessions`                     | Access credential                | Returns a bounded cursor page of the caller's active sessions without token material.                          |
| `DELETE /auth/sessions/{sessionId}`      | Access credential                | Revokes one session owned by the caller.                                                                       |

Unauthorized and forbidden resources may return `404 NOT_FOUND` where concealing
existence prevents enumeration. Authentication failures use stable machine codes such
as `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, `INVALID_OR_EXPIRED_TOKEN`, `SESSION_REVOKED`, and
`FORBIDDEN`; messages never distinguish unknown emails from incorrect passwords.

Invitation and password-reset email links place the raw token in the URL fragment, not
the query string. Public Web reads the fragment, replaces the URL before rendering or
telemetry, and submits the token in a POST body over HTTPS.

OpenAPI documents retry behavior for every state-changing route. Logout and owned
session revocation are idempotent. Clients serialize refresh, invitation acceptance,
and reset completion and do not automatically replay them after an unknown outcome;
refresh ambiguity falls back to login, while a consumed invitation/reset flow directs
the user to normal login with the password they just established. Secret-issuing
responses are never persisted in the core idempotency store merely to make replay
possible.

## 12. Notification Boundary

Identity owns credential state and message intent, not provider details or future
scheduling. It exposes an `IdentityNotificationPort` for workspace invitation and
password-reset delivery. The initial adapter validates and sends through the existing
`EmailProvider`; tests use a fake. `notifications-automation` may later implement the
same port asynchronously without moving token or account ownership.

Email idempotency keys derive from the invitation/reset record ID and message purpose.
Raw tokens may appear only in the outbound provider command created at the last
possible moment. Provider responses are validated and never copied into client errors.

## 13. Configuration

After D1–D5 approval, backend configuration adds allowlisted values for credential
lifetimes, password-cost parameters, auth rate limits, and cookie policy. Defaults are
allowed only in development/test; staging/production must fail fast if required secret
or origin settings are absent.

No auth secret is public. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` and `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` remain limited to API
base URLs and non-secret identifiers. Android secure storage requires the approved Expo
module and must never fall back to AsyncStorage.

## 14. Project Structure

```text
wedding-be/
├── prisma/                         # identity schema and forward migrations
├── src/modules/identity-access/
│   ├── account/                    # account, credential, and role services
│   ├── session/                    # access/refresh issuance and rotation
│   ├── workspace-invitation/       # invitation state and acceptance
│   ├── authorization/              # actor and consultation-access contracts
│   ├── password-reset/             # reset lifecycle
│   ├── identity.router.ts          # HTTP composition only
│   └── identity.schemas.ts         # Zod/OpenAPI boundaries
└── tests/integration/identity-access/

wedding-web/
├── app/(auth)/                     # login, invitation acceptance, reset
├── app/(couple)/                   # restricted/full shells only
└── src/features/identity-access/   # session store and auth UI

wedding-manage-web/
├── app/(auth)/                     # Manager/Staff login and reset
└── src/features/identity-access/   # session store and route guards

wedding-app/
├── src/app/(auth)/                 # Couple login/reset routes
└── src/features/identity-access/   # SecureStore session adapter
```

Route files remain thin; UI bodies live outside router directories. Domain code does
not import Express, Prisma-generated input types, Next.js, or Expo.

## 15. Code and Contract Style

- Strict TypeScript, ESM, kebab-case filenames, PascalCase types, camelCase values.
- Inputs and outputs are separate types; IDs for different concepts are not silently
  interchangeable.
- Schemas are strict and reject undocumented fields.
- State transitions are explicit functions and conditional database writes, not
  arbitrary enum assignment.
- Public API schemas are registered once and generated into OpenAPI/client types.
- New API fields are additive; breaking changes require a separately approved version
  plan.

## 16. Testing Strategy

### 16.1 Unit and mutation-sensitive tests

- Token generation/hashing never persists or logs raw values.
- Password verification covers correct, incorrect, malformed, and parameter-version
  paths with deterministic test doubles around costly crypto where appropriate.
- Policy tables exhaustively cover role and access-level allow/deny outcomes.
- Invitation, refresh, reset, and promotion transition guards cover every terminal
  state and invalid transition.
- Tests must fail when an authorization condition is inverted or removed.

### 16.2 PostgreSQL integration and concurrency tests

- Concurrent invitation acceptance has exactly one winner/session.
- Reissue racing acceptance produces either accepted-old or superseded-old, never both.
- Concurrent refresh has one rotation winner; replay revokes the family.
- Concurrent promotion stores one `FULL` transition and one audit fact.
- Promotion atomically upserts the `COUPLE` role without duplicating the account or
  consultation access record.
- Password reset completion is single-use and revokes every active session.
- Account-retention tests cover premature eligibility, multiple linked business
  records, active holds, idempotent facts, and due anonymization/erasure.
- Unique normalized email, invitation, role, session, and payment-source constraints are
  exercised against real PostgreSQL.

### 16.3 Contract and client tests

- OpenAPI covers success, validation, authentication, authorization, throttling, and
  generic enumeration-safe errors.
- Generated client schemas remain identical across all three clients.
- Public Web verifies fragment removal, memory-only access credentials, refresh-cookie
  behavior, restricted/full route presentation, and logout.
- Management Web verifies Manager/Staff route presentation but still expects backend
  denials for forged roles.
- Android verifies SecureStore-only refresh persistence, process restore, rotation, and
  logout deletion.
- Cross-module contract fixtures prove `RESTRICTED` is denied from every ACC-004
  capability and `FULL` alone is insufficient without resource ownership.

### 16.4 Requirement-to-test matrix

| Requirement | Planned automated evidence                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| ACC-002     | Invitation expiry/hash/consume unit tests; atomic acceptance integration test; Web fragment/token-leak test.             |
| ACC-003     | Consultation access policy table; restricted timeline/proposal contract fixture; cross-consultation IDOR denial.         |
| ACC-004     | Deny matrix for media, invitation, guest, seating, print, and operations capability contracts.                           |
| ACC-005     | Concurrent idempotent promotion integration test; same account/access IDs before and after promotion.                    |
| ACC-006     | Expired/revoked/superseded/consumed invitation tests; audit and consultation reference preservation.                     |
| ACC-007     | Middleware tests against forged client roles, revoked sessions, stale access, wrong consultation, and disabled accounts. |

## 17. Privacy, Retention, and Audit

| Data                          | Classification              | Purpose                                     | Approved retention                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Email/display name            | PII                         | Login, invitation delivery, account support | Active account lifetime; for disabled accounts, 365 days after the last linked business record becomes terminal, then delete/anonymize unless held |
| IP/user-agent/device label    | PII                         | Abuse defense and session recognition       | Session lifetime plus 90 days                                                                                                                      |
| Password verifier             | Sensitive credential        | Authentication                              | Until replacement/account erasure; never export                                                                                                    |
| Token hash                    | Sensitive security metadata | Single-use/replay detection                 | Per D6 terminal retention                                                                                                                          |
| Raw token/password            | Secret                      | One request/provider handoff only           | Never persist or log                                                                                                                               |
| Role/access/promotion history | Security/audit data         | Authorization and dispute evidence          | Pseudonymize account references when D6 account erasure runs; keep the minimum non-PII evidence required by the owning business record             |

Audit actions include login success/failure aggregate, logout, session revoke, refresh
reuse, password reset completion, invitation issue/reissue/revoke/accept, account status
change, role change, and Couple access promotion. Metadata is allowlisted and excludes
email, IP, user-agent, token hashes, raw provider responses, and message bodies unless a
later privacy review explicitly approves a pseudonymous field.

## 18. Observability

- Counters cover login outcomes, invitation outcomes, refresh outcomes, authorization
  denials by stable reason, and password-reset requests/completions.
- Metrics contain no account ID, consultation ID, email, IP, session ID, or token.
- Logs use event names and request IDs; the existing redactor remains defense in depth,
  not permission to log bodies.
- Alerts/operational thresholds are finalized in `release-demo`; this module supplies
  the stable low-cardinality signals.

## 19. Commands and Verification

Backend focused commands:

```powershell
npm run db:generate
npm run db:migrate:deploy
npm run test:unit -- identity-access
npm run test:integration -- identity-access
npm run test:contract
npm run api:check
npm run test:coverage
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm run build
npm run audit:ci
```

Client commands in each affected repository:

```powershell
npm run api:check
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm run test:coverage
npm run build
```

Expo additionally runs `npx expo-doctor` and `npm run audit:ci`. Every dependency
change begins with script-disabled review and ends with a clean `npm ci`.

## 20. Boundaries

### Always

- Validate every external auth input and verify authorization for every protected
  resource.
- Store only password/token hashes and use constant-time comparison.
- Make invitation, reset, refresh, and promotion transitions atomic and auditable.
- Use generic public errors and `Cache-Control: no-store` on auth responses.
- Revoke sessions on password reset, account disable, and refresh reuse.
- Derive rate-limit IPs from the direct socket unless an explicit trusted-proxy policy
  has been validated for the deployment topology.
- Test actual denials, concurrency, expiry boundaries, and token redaction.

### Ask first

- Change auth mechanism/provider, password policy, token transport, lifetimes, cookie
  flags, CORS, role grants, rate limits, or PII retention.
- Add a public registration flow, MFA, social identity, Redis/queue infrastructure, or
  another external provider.
- Permit more than one backend replica before shared security controls exist.
- Add a new PII field or send identity data to a third party.

### Never

- Trust role, account, consultation, payment, or access-level claims from a client.
- Store a raw password, invitation, reset, access, or refresh credential.
- Put credentials in URL queries, logs, metrics, audit metadata, browser storage, Git,
  or error responses.
- Treat hidden UI, decoded token fields, email possession after bootstrap, or a
  successful historical payment as sufficient current authorization.
- Create a second Couple account or consultation during promotion.

## 21. Success Criteria

1. ACC-002 through ACC-007 each map to explicit automated evidence.
2. Invitation acceptance is atomic, single-use, expiry-aware, and establishes a real
   revocable session without persisting the raw token.
3. Access and refresh credentials rotate/revoke as specified; refresh replay is
   detected and contained.
4. Passwords and reset credentials follow the approved cryptographic, throttling, and
   enumeration-safe policy.
5. Manager, Staff, restricted prospect, and full Couple access are backend-enforced
   from current state with cross-resource IDOR tests.
6. Deposit promotion is idempotent, monotonic, audited, and preserves the existing
   account and consultation access identity.
7. The OpenAPI contract and three generated clients remain deterministic and current.
8. Public Web, Management Web, and Android implement only presentation/session
   transport; they cannot grant a role or access level.
9. Auth logs, metrics, audit records, URLs, and client persistence contain no raw
   credential or unapproved PII.
10. All repository quality, PostgreSQL, contract, browser, Expo, and dependency-audit
    gates pass before implementation approval.

## 22. Approval Record

Checkpoint H1 approved D1 through D7 as written on 2026-10-03:

1. Approve first-party opaque-token auth, or choose an external auth provider/JWT.
2. Approve the Web cookie/in-memory and Android SecureStore transport split.
3. Approve the 10-minute / 30-day idle / 90-day absolute session policy.
4. Approve the 72-hour invitation and 3-reissues-per-24-hours policy.
5. Approve password length, scrypt, and throttling recommendations.
6. Approve the draft metadata periods and the 365-day disabled-account
   deletion/anonymization rule; `release-demo` must still fix backup purge timing and
   the legal/financial hold operator procedure.
7. Approve the existing-account invitation behavior requiring the existing password.

The approval authorizes the ordered IA-01 through IA-17 implementation plan. Any change
to the approved decisions or stop conditions still requires project-owner review.
````
