````text
# Specification: Seating Plan

- Status: **Approved specification — module plan and implementation acceptance pending**
- Approved: 2026-10-06 by the project owner (approval record: baseline Section 21.9)
- Module ID: `seating-plan` (`SPEC-07`)
- Contract baseline: `WEDDING-CONTRACT-1@1.1.0`
- Inherited baseline: `WEDDING-CONTRACT-1@1.0.0` (historical contract)
- Accepted amendment: baseline Section 21
- Initial owner role: C (member name to be assigned)
- Team execution contract: [`docs/team-implementation.md`](./docs/team-implementation.md)
- Requirement ownership: SEA-003 through SEA-008
- Depends on: `venue-catalog`, `booking-lifecycle`, `guest-rsvp`
- Consumers: `invitation-studio`, `staff-operations`, `analytics-dashboard`

## 1. Purpose and hard boundary

This module selects a capacity-compatible fixed catalog layout and applies guest-group
labels/colors to its stable tables. It owns seating-plan revision/status and no geometry.
It never assigns a household, person, or seat; creates/moves/resizes tables; changes a
layout range; or changes guest-group definitions.

## 2. State and immutable reference contract

A plan stores `seatingPlanId`, exact `layoutTemplateVersionId`, stable
`layoutTableId` labels, expected-attendance snapshot, and monotonic revision number.
States are `DRAFT`, `CONFIRMED`, and `REQUIRES_REVIEW`.

```text
DRAFT -> CONFIRMED
| |
| +-> REQUIRES_REVIEW -> CONFIRMED
+--------+------------------------------> replacement DRAFT
```

A selected layout is eligible only when booking planning headcount is in its immutable
range. An out-of-range headcount or retired layout changes a confirmed plan to
`REQUIRES_REVIEW`; labels/groups remain visible. Reconfirmation needs a compatible
layout or an audited Manager exception. Layout change may remap labels but never deletes
guest-group definitions.

## 3. Produced contracts

```ts
interface SeatingPlanReader {
  requireCurrentPlan(bookingId: string): Promise<{
    seatingPlanId: string;
    revisionId: string;
    status: 'DRAFT' | 'CONFIRMED' | 'REQUIRES_REVIEW';
    layoutTemplateVersionId: string;
    expectedAttendees: number;
    labels: readonly { layoutTableId: string; guestGroupId: string; colorSnapshot: string }[];
  }>;
  resolveRevision(revisionId: string): Promise<{
    bookingId: string;
    layoutTemplateVersionId: string;
    labels: readonly { layoutTableId: string; guestGroupId: string; colorSnapshot: string }[];
  }>;
}
```

Outputs are immutable snapshots. The reader never converts a current catalog geometry
lookup into a historical revision. Staff operations consumes only required group-label
guidance, not raw geometry.

## 4. Consumed contracts and printable registry

| Provider          | Contract                                     | Use                                                      |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| venue-catalog     | exact layout-version resolution              | Filter/rank and safely render restaurant-owned geometry. |
| booking-lifecycle | confirmed event context and headcount events | Gate access and check current planned count.             |
| guest-rsvp        | `GuestPlanningReader`                        | Resolve active group IDs/names/colors.                   |
| invitation-studio | `PrintableSeatingContentRegistry`            | Register/invalidate immutable render snapshot.           |

On confirm, resolve the exact layout, build the safe render snapshot, digest it, then
call `registerConfirmed` idempotently by seating revision. A higher revision wins;
changed digest is conflict. Invalidation wins for the same revision number; a
reconfirmation always creates a higher revision. On invalidation call `markRequiresReview`. This preserves
the acyclic dependency: invitation never makes a live seating call during print approval.

The module emits `seating.plan-confirmed` and `seating.plan-requires-review` v1.

## 5. Authorization, HTTP, and acceptance

Full Couple accounts select/label their booking's plan; Managers can perform a documented
exception with a reason; Staff see only assigned operational group guidance. Restricted,
public, and guest-link actors cannot access a plan. Specified routes are
`/bookings/{bookingId}/seating-plans` and explicit select/label/confirm/exception
actions. Writes use expected revision and `Idempotency-Key`. No generated API operation
permits table geometry or individual placement mutation.

Tests prove SEA-003–008: range selection, no geometry mutation, no person/seat
assignment, stale headcount event rejection, exception audit, printable registration
ordering, and preservation of an approved printable revision after later seating edits.

## 6. Confirmation and revision rules

A label is `{layoutTableId, guestGroupId}`; clients never submit authoritative group
name/color or geometry. The server resolves active group display values, snapshots them
in a new immutable plan revision, and checks the table belongs to the exact selected
layout/hall. Each table has zero or one group label; one group may label multiple tables.
Unlabelled tables are allowed; no aggregate per-group seat claim is inferred.

New selection requires an active current published layout for the booking hall.
Already selected historical versions retain immutable geometry. Confirming/reconfirming
an existing version additionally requires `VenueSelectionEligibilityReader` to prove
the template/hall has not retired; supersession alone is not retirement. This is a
accepted additive venue-owned port, separately scheduled without altering VC tasks.
A confirmed read/print boundary revalidates retirement; a five-minute reconciliation
sweep handles dormant plans. Guest headcount updates use bookingRevision high-water
marks, not timestamps, and the confirmation command rechecks current headcount.

Default range comparison is inclusive `minGuests <= planningHeadcount <= maxGuests`.
Manager exception requires reason 10–500, exact layout/plan/headcount revisions, and
an immutable exception record. It may override the template minimum/maximum only within
active hall maximum and physical total seat capacity; it cannot override a retired hall/
layout or mutate geometry. A later headcount change invalidates the old exception and
requires an explicit new one. A plan may be saved as draft with total zero; confirmation
requires positive planning count.

Every select/label edit produces a new immutable DRAFT revision while preserving the
prior confirmed historical revision. Reconfirming creates a greater revision number;
it never re-registers an invalidated revision as eligible. Layout change automatically
preserves labels only for stable table IDs also present in the new version; all other
remaps are explicit mappings and may drop labels without deleting guest groups.

## 7. Registry atomicity and guidance provider

Confirmation/invalidation and invitation registry eligibility changes share the
booking-bound application unit-of-work. Lock order follows the team guide. A failed
registry update rolls back that state transition and confirmation cannot claim success.
Registry invalidation is terminal at equal revision number. Delayed older registration
is a no-op acknowledgement; same ID/different digest is conflict. Existing printable
revisions remain unchanged after invalidation.

Retirement/headcount checks occur before every confirmation and print approval boundary
through the owner port; background delivery is not the sole check. A print approval and
headcount/retirement revalidation are serialized so either valid snapshot approval wins
first or the invalidation blocks a later approval. Venue lifecycle eligibility reads
hold the owner shared lock until commit; retirement uses its exclusive lock, as defined
in baseline Section 21.10. Booking serialization alone is not a venue-retirement lock.

Additive `SeatingGuidanceReader` returns group-labelled table labels and plan status for
a booking only, with no person/household/seat mapping:

```typescript
interface SeatingGuidanceReader {
  getGuidance(
    bookingId: string,
    context: ContractContext,
  ): Promise<
    Readonly<{
      seatingPlanRevisionId: string | null;
      status: 'DRAFT' | 'CONFIRMED' | 'REQUIRES_REVIEW' | 'ABSENT';
      groups: readonly Readonly<{
        guestGroupId: string;
        groupName: string;
        color: string;
        tableLabels: readonly string[];
      }>[];
    }>
  >;
}
```

No plan is a successful `ABSENT` response with an empty group list, so Staff can still
check in arrivals. Unconfirmed/requires-review guidance is clearly labelled provisional;
Staff must not present it as a reserved table.

## 8. HTTP schemas, errors, and independent slices

| Method/path                                             | Strict input                                                                          | Result                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| GET /bookings/{id}/seating-layout-options               | Optional cursor                                                                       | Current compatible/ranked catalog versions and warnings from current planning count. |
| POST /bookings/{id}/seating-plans                       | layoutTemplateVersionId, expectedBookingRevision                                      | DRAFT revision with immutable safe geometry preview.                                 |
| POST /bookings/{id}/seating-plans/{planId}/revisions    | expectedRevision, labels[{layoutTableId, guestGroupId}], optional layoutVersion/remap | New DRAFT; no geometry fields allowed.                                               |
| POST /bookings/{id}/seating-plans/{planId}/confirmation | expectedRevision, expectedBookingRevision                                             | New CONFIRMED revision + registered digest, or conflict.                             |
| POST /management/seating-plans/{planId}/exceptions      | expectedRevision, expectedBookingRevision, reason                                     | Manager-only exact headcount exception and confirmed new revision.                   |
| GET /bookings/{id}/seating-plans/{planId}               | no body                                                                               | Immutable selected revision plus current validity and warnings.                      |

Errors are `SEATING_REVISION_STALE`, `HEADCOUNT_OUTSIDE_LAYOUT_RANGE`,
`LAYOUT_RETIRED`, `TABLE_NOT_IN_LAYOUT`, `GUEST_GROUP_UNAVAILABLE`,
`EXCEPTION_EXCEEDS_PHYSICAL_CAPACITY` (409); strict geometry/person assignment fields
are 422; unowned booking is concealed 404.

| Slice                               | Can run alongside                      | Real dependency                                                         |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Range/group/remap/domain rules      | Guest and Notifications implementation | Frozen provider fixtures.                                               |
| Plan persistence/guidance           | Staff domain/UI fixtures               | Serialized migration lane.                                              |
| Confirm/registry/shared transaction | Invitation registry implementation     | Real venue eligibility, guest/booking, registry/UoW before integration. |
| Web/App group-label UI              | Own HTTP work using local fixture      | Committed generated API for adapters; responsive read-only geometry.    |

Proposed waves: compatibility/remapping; plan persistence/revisions;
confirmation/exception/registry/guidance; HTTP/OpenAPI; client slices; acceptance.
SEA-003/006 tests include boundary equality, zero count, retirement versus supersession,
exception revalidation, concurrent headcount/confirm and invalidation/print approval.
SEA-004/005/007/008 tests cover stable group IDs, no person/geometry writes, remap
visibility and accessible keyboard alternatives to label drag.

Registration includes `validityProof` with exact min/max, physical seat capacity,
booking revision/headcount and optional approved Manager exception. Print rechecks
this proof against current booking/venue facts even before invalidation messages arrive.
See baseline Section 21.10.
````

````text
# Specification: Staff Operations

- Status: **Approved specification — module plan and implementation acceptance pending**
- Approved: 2026-10-06 by the project owner (approval record: baseline Section 21.9)
- Module ID: `staff-operations` (`SPEC-08`)
- Contract baseline: `WEDDING-CONTRACT-1@1.1.0`
- Inherited baseline: `WEDDING-CONTRACT-1@1.0.0` (historical contract)
- Accepted amendment: baseline Section 21
- Initial owner role: C (member name to be assigned)
- Team execution contract: [`docs/team-implementation.md`](./docs/team-implementation.md)
- Requirement ownership: CHK-001 through CHK-008
- Depends on: `identity-access`, `booking-lifecycle`, `guest-rsvp`, `seating-plan`
- Consumers: `analytics-dashboard`

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

This module owns event assignments and an append-only actual-attendance ledger. It lets
assigned Staff search an invitation household by name, optionally disambiguate safely by
phone, record several arrivals, and record auditable corrections. It does not own
household/RSVP truth, expected counts, guest groups, seating selection, or payment.

## 2. Attendance and assignment contract

An assignment binds a Staff account to a booking/event scope and current status. An
arrival has `arrivalId`, household, positive count, event time, actor, and immutable
request identity. A correction has `attendanceCorrectionId`, referenced prior evidence,
signed delta/reason, actor, and time. Neither arrival nor correction is hard-deleted.

Actual count is the sum of effective arrivals and corrections. It may exceed expected
count: success returns `hasOverExpectedWarning: true`, never a blocking error.

```ts
interface AttendanceReader {
  getHouseholdAttendance(invitationHouseholdId: string): Promise<{
    expectedAttendees: number;
    actualAttendees: number;
    hasOverExpectedWarning: boolean;
  }>;
  getBookingAttendance(bookingId: string): Promise<{
    actualAttendees: number;
    byGuestGroup: readonly { guestGroupId: string; actualAttendees: number }[];
  }>;
}
```

## 3. Dependencies and events

| Provider          | Contract                        | Use                                                         |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| identity-access   | current role/actor              | Require current Staff or Manager role, never a client role. |
| booking-lifecycle | confirmed event context         | Validate assignment/event scope.                            |
| guest-rsvp        | `requireHouseholdForOperations` | Minimum household/group/expected/note data only.            |
| seating-plan      | current plan reader             | Group guidance only; never infer personal table/seat.       |

It emits `attendance.arrival-recorded` and `attendance.correction-recorded` v1.
Events include baseline minimum IDs/counts/times only; no phone or operational note.

## 4. Authorization, HTTP, and concurrency

Staff needs both current role and current assignment; Manager override is explicit and
audited. Assignment lifecycle is Manager-controlled. Public, Couple, restricted prospect,
and generic/personalized QR paths cannot search or record attendance.

Specified routes are `/management/events/{bookingId}/assignments`,
`/staff/events/{bookingId}/households/search`, household attendance reads, arrivals,
and correction commands. Search limits result fields, uses controlled name matching, and
reveals phone only when policy allows disambiguation. Mutations require an idempotency
key. Duplicate arrival intent replays once; concurrent different arrivals both count.
Errors include `EVENT_ASSIGNMENT_REQUIRED`, `ARRIVAL_COUNT_INVALID`,
`ATTENDANCE_CORRECTION_CONFLICT`, and non-blocking `OVER_EXPECTED_ATTENDANCE`.

## 5. Acceptance

Prove CHK-001–008 with direct backend denial tests, duplicate-name handling, multi-arrival
sum, warning-not-block behavior, correction history, assignment revocation race, and
privacy-minimized search. Integrate real guest/seating providers and prove reporting
cannot derive personal seat occupancy.

## 6. Staff provisioning, assignment, and operational window

Staff operations exposes the Manager provisioning workflow while identity owns
`StaffAccountProvisioner` and password setup. Provisioning never accepts a role field
or stores password/verifier/token. Existing normalized email identity is reused; a
separate Couple role/access must survive Staff disable. Disabling Staff operational access
revokes Staff authority and applicable sessions through the identity port and revokes
active event assignments through this module's audited commands.

An assignment is `ACTIVE | REVOKED`, unique by booking/account with revision and history.
Current actor role and assignment are rechecked inside every write. Manager override
requires reason 10–500. Event window defaults to start − two hours through event end +
12 hours; regular arrivals outside it return `CHECK_IN_WINDOW_CLOSED`. Manager may
record an explicit reasoned late arrival/correction, including after completion.

Attendance uses immutable positive arrival counts (1–100) and correction deltas
(−100 through +100, nonzero) linked to a specific arrival. Effective count for any arrival
and total household cannot fall below zero. Each correction has expectedLedgerRevision,
reason 10–500, acting account and event time. Staff may correct only their own arrivals
while assigned and within the window; Manager may correct all with explicit audit.

A household's attendance group is snapshotted from the first valid arrival; subsequent
arrivals/corrections retain it. If current guest group changes, return a
`GUEST_GROUP_CHANGED` guidance warning while preserving historical grouping. Do not
silently move previous attendance to a new group. The ledger revision is monotonically
increasing and allocated atomically with arrival/correction/reporting change.

## 7. Operational HTTP request/response contract

| Method/path                                                     | Input                                                            | Result                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| POST /management/staff-accounts                                 | email; durable command key                                       | accountId/setupRequired via identity; Manager only.                                     |
| POST /management/staff-accounts/{id}/operational-access         | enabled, reason                                                  | Identity-owned role/session change plus assignment reconciliation.                      |
| GET/POST /management/events/{bookingId}/assignments             | List or staffAccountId                                           | Current assignment/revision; active Staff identity required.                            |
| POST /management/events/{bookingId}/assignments/{id}/revocation | expectedRevision, reason                                         | REVOKED with retained history.                                                          |
| GET /staff/events/{bookingId}/households/search                 | name?/phone?, cursor?, limit 1–50                                | Guest operations search joined with actualAttendees/warning and seating group guidance. |
| POST /staff/events/{bookingId}/households/{id}/arrivals         | attendeeCount, eventTime?, Manager override reason when required | arrivalId/ledgerRevision/cumulative actual count/warnings; 201 even when over expected. |
| POST /staff/events/{bookingId}/households/{id}/corrections      | arrivalId, delta, expectedLedgerRevision, reason                 | New correctionId/ledgerRevision/effective count; never overwrite arrival.               |
| GET /staff/events/{bookingId}/households/{id}/attendance        | cursor when history requested                                    | Minimum summary and authorized ledger history.                                          |

Name/phone query fields are redacted from access logs and metrics. Backend joins guest
search and attendance using returned household IDs, not direct guest repository access.
PhoneLast4 is the only contact output on this search surface. Guest names/notes are private
operational output, never events/analytics labels. Missing seating returns provisional/
ABSENT guidance and does not block arrival.

When actual count exceeds expected count, response is successful with
`warnings: [{code: 'OVER_EXPECTED_ATTENDANCE', expectedAttendees, actualAttendees}]`.
This code is never placed in the HTTP error envelope. Stale correction is
`ATTENDANCE_CORRECTION_CONFLICT` (409), assignment denial 403/concealed 404 as scoped,
invalid/negative-effective counts 422. Revocation racing an arrival has a serialized
winner; an already committed arrival remains evidence.

## 8. Reporting, concurrency, and independent implementation

`AttendanceReportingReader` publishes absolute household actual totals and snapshotted
group ID at a source fence (baseline Section 21). Corrections update one authoritative
ledger; analytics never sums event deltas without an idempotent source checkpoint.

| Slice                               | Can overlap                                               | Requires real provider                                                |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Assignment/arrival/correction rules | Seating and Notifications domain work                     | Frozen current-role/window/household/guidance DTOs.                   |
| PostgreSQL ledger/repository        | Other modules in separate file lanes                      | Serialized migration order and concurrent append/correction tests.    |
| Staff search and Web components     | Guest search/Seating implementation with conforming fakes | Real search scope + identity/assignment + guidance before acceptance. |
| Provisioning disable/revocation     | Identity-owned adapter slice                              | Real identity role/session behavior, no fake-only security closure.   |

Proposed waves: provisioning/assignments; attendance ledger;
search/guidance/reporting; HTTP/OpenAPI; Staff Web; acceptance.

| Requirements    | Focused proof                                                                                               |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CHK-001/002     | Duplicate names, name/phone ranking, exact booking scope, expected/actual/group/color/safe note.            |
| CHK-003–006     | Two arrivals counted once each, same-key replay, over-expected 201, correction race/nonnegative history.    |
| CHK-007/008     | Group guidance with absent/stale seating, no personal table reservation, QR carries no operation authority. |
| Security/source | Role/assignment revocation race; Couple role survives Staff disable; real read-port/report rebuild.         |
````

```text
# Specification: Notifications and Automation

- Status: **Approved specification — module plan and implementation acceptance pending**
- Approved: 2026-10-06 by the project owner (approval record: baseline Section 21.9)
- Module ID: `notifications-automation` (`SPEC-09`)
- Contract baseline: `WEDDING-CONTRACT-1@1.1.0`
- Inherited baseline: `WEDDING-CONTRACT-1@1.0.0` (historical contract)
- Accepted amendment: baseline Section 21
- Initial owner role: Unassigned (next allocation round)
- Team execution contract: [`docs/team-implementation.md`](./docs/team-implementation.md)
- Requirement ownership: OPS-001 and OPS-002
- Depends on: `identity-access`, `booking-lifecycle`, `payments-billing`, `invitation-studio`, `guest-rsvp`
- Consumers: operational views only

## 1. Purpose and ownership

This module consumes durable integration facts and owns notification preferences,
schedule evaluation, notification intents, delivery attempts, retries, dead-letter
records, and operational delivery status. It never becomes the source of booking,
payment, print, RSVP, or attendance truth and it never publishes delivery status as a
domain fact that another module may use as authorization or settlement proof.

## 2. Delivery and privacy contract

One intent has a stable `notificationIntentId`, source `eventId`, purpose, recipient,
channel, template version, scheduled time, and state. Attempts record provider outcome
without overwriting prior evidence. The deduplication key is
`(eventId, channel, recipientId, templateVersion)`; retry reuses the same intent.

A provider timeout is an unknown outcome that must be reconciled, not a signal to create
another intent. Message inputs contain only references and purpose-specific minimal data:
never raw credentials in ordinary event/render payloads, private media attachments, full guest lists, payment secrets,
phones beyond a channel's delivery requirement, or complete operational notes.

## 3. Consumed events and output boundary

| Producer          | Required event inputs                                                             |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| identity-access   | `identity.consultation-access-promoted`                                           |
| booking-lifecycle | timeline review/approval/supersession, deposit eligible, cancellation, completion |
| payments-billing  | payment succeeded, receivable accepted, refund recorded                           |
| invitation-studio | publication change, print quotation/approval/ready                                |
| guest-rsvp        | RSVP and expected-attendance change                                               |

The exact handler names, recipient derivation, template version, and schedule cadence
remain local decisions but each handler must be explicit, versioned, and tested against
the frozen event schema. Consumer processing is idempotent by `eventId`, compares
event version/aggregate sequence where supplied, and safely discards or reconciles
delayed old facts.

## 4. Authorization, channels, and HTTP

Only authorized Manager/Couple settings surfaces may change preferences for their own
scope. No public, guest-link, or Staff route can enumerate notification recipients or
delivery records. Management operations may inspect redacted operational status and
requeue a dead-letter intent only with audit evidence.

Email delivery uses the platform provider boundary. Android push is limited to a
registered, authorized device token managed under identity/device policy. Specified routes
cover scoped preferences and authorized delivery-status reads; workers and provider
webhooks remain internal. Every mutation uses idempotency and the platform error
envelope.

## 5. Acceptance

Prove each required OPS-001 trigger renders minimal content, does not leak protected
data, deduplicates duplicate events, preserves intent under retry/timeout, handles
out-of-order facts, honors revocation/preferences, and makes operational failures
observable without message content. Final acceptance uses real producer outbox events
and one configured email/push test path without treating delivery as a business outcome.

## 6. Trigger, recipient, channel, and scheduling contract

| Trigger / source                                                   | Recipient                                                                        | Channel / exact schedule                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Workspace invitation/password reset via `IdentityNotificationPort` | Intended account email from identity                                             | Transactional email at issuance; privileged credential path below.                                         |
| booking.timeline-review-requested                                  | Other approving party; current consultation Couple account or Manager recipients | Email; Android push only for FULL registered account.                                                      |
| booking.timeline-approved/superseded/deposit-eligible              | Owning Couple + designated Manager operational recipients                        | Email and enabled Android push; dedup by source event/channel/template.                                    |
| billing.payment-succeeded/refund-recorded                          | Owning Couple + Manager finance recipient                                        | Transactional email; payment settlement only, no raw provider payload.                                     |
| invitation.print-quotation-issued/approved/ready                   | Owning Couple; Manager print recipient when action needs handling                | Email + enabled push with exact order/revision references.                                                 |
| Personalized invitation via guest delivery port                    | Explicit household email, never inferred from phone                              | Transactional email; approved public content and scoped link only.                                         |
| Media cutoff due read                                              | Owning Couple                                                                    | One reminder 24 hours before cutoff for policyRevision.                                                    |
| RSVP deadline due read                                             | Owning Couple                                                                    | One reminder 24 hours before deadline for deadlineRevision.                                                |
| D-3 due booking read                                               | Owning Couple + operational Manager recipient                                    | Event start − 72 hours using snapshotted local shift/time.                                                 |
| Completion due booking read                                        | No external recipient needed for command                                         | Worker calls booking-owned completeDue at event end + 12 hours; consumes resulting event for notification. |

Manager recipients come from an explicitly configured approved operational recipient
registry resolved through identity. No hard-coded developer email. Active account/
delivery preference is revalidated before send; a revoked/archived account does not get
ordinary messages. Transactional credential/security/payment messages cannot be muted;
reminders and informational push/email may be disabled by scoped preference.

Worker runs every 60 seconds, claims at most 100 due intents with a two-minute lease,
and reclaims only with persisted provider outcome/reconciliation rules. Scheduled intent
key is `(bookingId, purpose, scheduleRevision, dueAt, channel, recipientId, templateVersion)`.
Each accepted due read is bounded/cursor-paged; handlers recheck current booking/deadline/
cutoff revision just before dispatch. Cancelled events suppress reminders and completion
commands. Missed D-3/deadline/cutoff reminders more than 24 hours late are marked
`SKIPPED_STALE`; future due reminders remain queued.

## 7. Credential delivery and private recipient boundaries

`IdentityNotificationPort` is explicitly consumed for workspace/password credentials,
and `PersonalizedInvitationDeliveryPort` is guest-owned for scoped invitation delivery.
The initial identity synchronous adapter may remain in place until this adapter passes
the same conformance suite; security-sensitive delivery is not inferred from
`identity.consultation-access-promoted`, which occurs after deposit.

Only these purpose-specific outbound commands may contain a transient link credential
at the final delivery boundary. If queued, credential content is encrypted using a
backend-only authenticated-encryption adapter, booking/purpose/intent AAD, versioned key,
and expiry no later than token expiry (maximum 72 hours). Never serialize plaintext into
outbox event, notification render data, log, API response history, audit, analytics,
or dead-letter display. Terminal ciphertext expires/is purged; record metadata remains.
Unknown send result keeps the same intent, ciphertext, and provider idempotency key.

`NotificationRecipientReader` resolves purpose-scoped active email by account ID.
Device tokens are owned here, private, and bound to current active account/session;
register/revoke never accepts another accountId as authority. Default limit five active
Android installations/account; new registration revokes any superseded token for the
same installation ID. On logout/account revocation, push dispatch rechecks identity and
session validity; invalid provider tokens are disabled.

## 8. Intent state, retry, and provider contract

Intent states are `QUEUED, IN_FLIGHT, DELIVERED, RETRYABLE_FAILED, UNKNOWN,
DEAD_LETTER, SKIPPED_STALE, CANCELLED`. Delivery evidence is append-only.
A stable provider idempotency key derives from intent UUID, channel, and template version.
Retry delays are one minute, five minutes, 30 minutes, two hours, then 12 hours;
maximum five retry attempts after the first. Permanent invalid destination/content
errors dead-letter immediately. Unknown result is reconciled using provider message ID/
idempotency status; if provider cannot query it, retain UNKNOWN for Manager resolution
rather than sending blindly after the provider's dedup retention expires.

One backend replica initially hosts the worker. Persisted claim/dedup still handles crash
and duplicate invocation. Worker lease expiry does not itself prove a send failed.
Requeue retains original intent identity; generating a second notification intent for the
same source/channel/recipient/template is prohibited.

## 9. HTTP and independent implementation

| Method/path                                      | Request                                                     | Result / authority                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| GET/PATCH /notifications/preferences             | Optional reminder email/push settings with expectedRevision | Own authenticated scope; no accountId role override.                         |
| POST /notifications/android-installations        | installationId, pushToken                                   | Private account/session-bound registration.                                  |
| DELETE /notifications/android-installations/{id} | expectedRevision                                            | Own token revocation.                                                        |
| GET /management/notifications                    | Purpose/state/cursor                                        | Manager redacted status only; no recipient address/token/ciphertext/content. |
| POST /management/notifications/{id}/requeue      | expectedRevision, reason                                    | Same intent retry after eligible outcome; never new money/booking effect.    |

Internal scheduler consumes `BookingAutomationPort`, `InvitationAutomationReader`,
and `GuestAutomationReader`. It owns no domain update except through those ports.
Push adapter errors are classified as retryable/permanent/unknown with no provider body
leakage. Core email/push doubles isolate tests from paid/network providers.

| Slice                                             | Can run alongside                      | Real dependency                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Intent/retry/channel adapter and scheduler engine | Seating/Staff/Analytics implementation | Frozen envelope/due/credential DTOs; core outbox lane.                      |
| Individual producer handler                       | Unrelated producer/module work         | That producer's event schema and recipient port, then real outbox evidence. |
| Credential/delivery adapter                       | Guest personalized-link implementation | Identity/guest actual token/revoke/expiry behavior before acceptance.       |
| Completion/deadline automation                    | Client screens and analytics           | Real due-list/complete command ports; time-controlled integration tests.    |

Proposed waves: durable intents/channel registry; credential/recipient/device adapters;
event handlers; due scheduler/reconciliation; settings/operations API/client; acceptance.

| Requirements/scope | Proof                                                                                                           |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| OPS-001            | Every table trigger has producer, recipient, schedule, real-provider fixture and redacted rendered content.     |
| OPS-002            | No plaintext credential/PII/media in ordinary events/logs/status; encrypted privileged credential path expires. |
| Automation         | Fake-clock deadline revision change, cancellation, restart, stale reminder, due completion replay.              |
| Delivery           | Duplicate outbox fact, concurrent claims, unknown timeout, dead-letter/requeue without second intent.           |
```

````text
# Specification: Analytics Dashboard

- Status: **Approved specification — module plan and implementation acceptance pending**
- Approved: 2026-10-06 by the project owner (approval record: baseline Section 21.9)
- Module ID: `analytics-dashboard` (`SPEC-10`)
- Contract baseline: `WEDDING-CONTRACT-1@1.1.0`
- Inherited baseline: `WEDDING-CONTRACT-1@1.0.0` (historical contract)
- Accepted amendment: baseline Section 21
- Initial owner role: Unassigned (next allocation round)
- Team execution contract: [`docs/team-implementation.md`](./docs/team-implementation.md)
- Requirement ownership: OPS-003 and OPS-004
- Depends on: `venue-catalog`, `booking-lifecycle`, `payments-billing`, `invitation-studio`, `guest-rsvp`, `seating-plan`, `staff-operations`
- Consumers: Management Web

## 1. Purpose and read-only boundary

This module provides Manager-only projections for KPIs, revenue, receivables, booking
status, hall utilization, menu popularity, print status, and expected-versus-actual
attendance by household and group. It owns projection/checkpoint metadata only. It never
writes domain state, counts draft quotations as receivables, recomputes provider money
truth, or infers exact table/seat occupancy.

## 2. Metric definitions and historical semantics

| Metric                            | Authoritative source                           | Non-negotiable interpretation                                 |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Revenue/paid/refunded/outstanding | payments ledger                                | Integer VND; accepted charge/payment/refund evidence only.    |
| Print receivable/status           | billing + invitation immutable revisions       | Draft/requested/quoted amount is not receivable.              |
| Booking status/utilization        | booking snapshots + catalog version references | Historical reports preserve event date/hall snapshot meaning. |
| Menu popularity                   | committed booking menu snapshot                | Never rewrite history from current catalog names/prices.      |
| Expected vs actual attendance     | guest expected revision + attendance ledger    | Group/household only; no personal seating inference.          |

Every result declares time window, timezone, refresh/checkpoint freshness, source
definition version, and filtering semantics. Local-date filters use
`Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`; storage/checkpoint times are UTC.

## 3. Inputs, projection behavior, and output contract

Sources are provider-approved read ports or baseline durable events. Every consumer is
idempotent by source event ID and stores a checkpoint/revision so delayed events cannot
replace newer projection state. Rebuild is deterministic from source facts and is an
authorized operational command, not a mutation of source records.

Specified Manager endpoints are `/management/analytics/overview`,
`/management/analytics/revenue`, `/management/analytics/bookings`,
`/management/analytics/attendance`, and `/management/analytics/print-orders`.
Responses are cursor/page or bounded aggregate results with a freshness field. They
never include raw guest phone, notes, access tokens, signed URLs, provider callback data,
or data from a booking the Manager is not authorized to see.

## 4. Security, audit, and acceptance

Manager role is checked in the backend on every view/export. Exports are approved only
for the minimum aggregate data required and are audited with filters and result size, not
row content. Dashboard cache keys must include Manager scope and query filters.

Acceptance proves each OPS-003/004 metric against known ledger/snapshot fixtures,
historical catalog changes, duplicate/out-of-order source events, source rebuild,
time-zone boundaries, Manager denial, PII minimization, and parity between API and
Management Web presentation. It completes only after real staff-attendance source data
exists.

## 5. Exact KPI definitions and source hand-off

| KPI                  | Formula and period meaning                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Gross cash received  | Sum PAYMENT ledger amounts whose settled occurredAt is inside the UTC-translated requested local-date range.                                                                               |
| Cash refunded        | Sum REFUND amounts whose recorded occurredAt is inside that same range.                                                                                                                    |
| Net cash revenue     | Gross cash received minus cash refunded for the cash period; never includes quotes or merely accepted charges.                                                                             |
| Receivables          | Sum latest provider outstandingVnd as of source fence for bookings whose eventDate is within requested event-date range.                                                                   |
| Credit balance       | Sum provider creditVnd for the same bookings; show separately, never hide it by clamping revenue.                                                                                          |
| Booking status count | Distinct bookingId by latest phase as of fence; filter uses eventDate, not confirmation or creation date.                                                                                  |
| Hall utilization     | Occupied confirmed/completed hall-date-shift slots divided by available active hall-date-shift slots for local event-date range. Cancelled/draft/awaiting-deposit do not occupy numerator. |
| Menu popularity      | Distinct confirmed/completed bookings by accepted snapshotted menuPackageId; optional tableCount sum shown as a separate metric.                                                           |
| Print status         | Count current print orders by state; accepted current commercial amount is presentation only, receivable comes from billing ledger.                                                        |
| Attendance           | Household expectation, planningContribution, actual ledger count, and actual − expectation; group totals aggregate their stable source group IDs.                                          |

No percent is produced when denominator is zero; return null with
`NO_AVAILABLE_SLOTS`. Utilization may be shown only if the catalog source can prove
active availability for each historical date/shift. The accepted
`VenueReportingReader` publishes the historical available-slot denominator;
current catalog names/active flags are not a substitute. If that source is unavailable,
return metric status `SOURCE_NOT_READY`, not a fabricated zero or current-state ratio.

Expected invited counts and RSVP planning contributions are displayed separately so a
declined invitation contributes zero to planning while its original household expectation
remains auditable. Actual attendance uses Staff's historical first-arrival group snapshot;
a later guest-group change is flagged and does not rewrite actual group history.
Household drill-down uses opaque household ID and approved display label only when
Manager private drill-down is requested; aggregate metrics never expose phone/note.

## 6. Read-port DTOs, checkpoints, and rebuild

Consume the accepted baseline ports `BookingReportingReader`,
`BillingReportingReader`, `InvitationReportingReader`, `GuestReportingReader`,
`AttendanceReportingReader`, and `VenueReportingReader`. Each supplies strict
readonly source rows with owner sequence/fence/cursor. Metric code does not import
Prisma/provider repositories. Domain events invalidate or enqueue refresh; authoritative
read pages supply missing history/details rather than inventing fields absent from events.

Refresh every 60 seconds and after invalidating facts. Advance a provider checkpoint only
after all pages through its fence are atomically applied. A source error preserves prior
projection/checkpoint and marks that metric stale. Projection metadata records each
owner's throughSequence/refreshedAt; there is no global comparison of different sequences.
A rebuild uses a shadow projection generation then atomically switches after catch-up;
readers never see half an empty rebuilt dashboard.

Retention defaults to permanent aggregate/projection facts without guest contacts.
Data subject display identity belongs to provider minimization/retention; analytics does
not create a new PII retention copy. Reporting rows never include raw operational notes,
contact values, signed URLs, token hashes, or provider callback payload.

## 7. HTTP result and filter contract

All analytics endpoints require current Manager role. Required filters:
`dateFrom, dateTo` as inclusive local YYYY-MM-DD (1–366 days);
optional `hallId, phase, menuPackageId` where applicable. Backend translates cash
ranges to half-open UTC instants [local midnight dateFrom, local midnight dateTo + 1 day).
Currency is fixed VND. Sorting is deterministic, list pageSize 1–100, default 20.

Every result contains:

```typescript
type AnalyticsMeta = Readonly<{
  metricDefinitionVersion: '1';
  timezone: 'Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh';
  dateFrom: string;
  dateTo: string;
  refreshedAt: string | null;
  sourceCheckpoints: readonly Readonly<{
    owner: string;
    throughSequence: number;
    refreshedAt: string;
  }>[];
  status: 'READY' | 'STALE' | 'SOURCE_NOT_READY';
}>;
```

Overview returns cash/receivable/credit/status counters with these metadata;
attendance returns cursor-paged household/group expectation/planning/actual/difference;
hall utilization returns numerator/denominator/rate/null-reason. A filter with no matching
rows is a successful empty result, distinct from missing source data. Exports use the
same definitions and Manager scope, bounded 10,000 rows; no formula-capable guest text
is emitted into spreadsheet cells without safe escaping.

## 8. Parallel work and acceptance evidence

| Slice                                  | Can run alongside                                   | Real dependency                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pure metric functions/DTO/schema tests | Staff/Notifications and source provider development | Known immutable fixtures and agreed formulas.                                                 |
| Individual source projector            | Other projectors/module screens                     | Its real paged reporting port at PROVIDER_READY.                                              |
| Management dashboard components        | Backend integration using local DTO fixtures        | Committed generated API before network adapter integration.                                   |
| Complete analytics acceptance          | Notifications need not be complete                  | Every required real reporting source, including attendance and historical venue availability. |

Proposed waves: formulas/source contracts; projection/checkpoint/rebuild;
Manager API/OpenAPI; dashboard/export presentation; acceptance (five).

OPS-003 tests cover decline/pending/accepted planning, two arrivals/correction, group
rename/change history, and household totals. OPS-004 tests include quoted amount excluded,
accepted print charge, cancellation credit, replacement charge, and fulfillment state.
Source tests include midnight boundaries, same record newer sequence then older,
duplicate refresh, paged fence concurrency, source failure, and atomic rebuild switch.
Revenue/receivable examples are checked against the payment SPEC's ledger fixtures,
not an independent dashboard calculation of billing obligations.
````

```text
# Specification: Release Demo

- Status: **Approved specification — module plan and implementation acceptance pending**
- Approved: 2026-10-06 by the project owner (approval record: baseline Section 21.9)
- Module ID: `release-demo` (`SPEC-11`)
- Contract baseline: `WEDDING-CONTRACT-1@1.1.0`
- Inherited baseline: `WEDDING-CONTRACT-1@1.0.0` (historical contract)
- Accepted amendment: baseline Section 21
- Initial owner role: Unassigned (next allocation round)
- Team execution contract: [`docs/team-implementation.md`](./docs/team-implementation.md)
- Requirement ownership: release verification, deployment, demo evidence, and rollback readiness
- Depends on: all preceding modules
- Consumers: project owner and demo reviewers

## 1. Purpose and boundary

This module owns no business state or alternate business rules. It composes accepted
public contracts into deterministic seed scenarios, deployment configuration, demo
script, monitoring/alert checks, evidence, and rollback procedure. It cannot paper over
an unaccepted provider with mocked client behavior.

## 2. Required release contract

A release candidate records:

- exact backend/client commit and generated OpenAPI digest;
- forward migration order and verified backup/rollback posture;
- environment-variable presence checks without secret values;
- deterministic idempotent demo seed keys that never overwrite Manager-managed data;
- Android EAS artifact identity, Web/API URLs, and health-check evidence;
- named owner, timestamp, result, and redacted evidence for each acceptance scenario.

The end-to-end journey must demonstrate consultation invitation, restricted timeline
collaboration, mutual approval, proven deposit/access promotion, media/invitation,
households/RSVP, seating invalidation/reconfirmation, print quote/charge, staff
multi-arrival check-in, notifications, and analytics. The generic QR must remain
non-personalized and non-authorizing throughout.

## 3. Deployment, verification, and rollback

Deployment runs forward-only database migrations in the serialized migration lane and
checks health/readiness before client rollout. The release script never runs seed data
automatically in production. A rollback plan distinguishes reversible client/service
deployment from irreversible schema/data migration; it specifies compatible forward fix
or restore point rather than destructive database rollback.

Required proof includes versioned API contract checks in all clients, migration from empty
and prior approved schema, focused security/redaction tests, smoke tests of provider
integrations, Android install/launch, monitoring/log checks, and a documented recovery
owner. No secret, token, raw PII, signed URL, or payment callback body is captured in
demo evidence.

## 4. Acceptance

Release acceptance requires every preceding module's provider and real integration gate,
all cross-module scenarios from the product requirements, no unresolved contract drift,
and an owner-reviewed demo/rollback checklist. Failure of a required provider, migration,
or privacy check blocks release; a visual workaround does not waive the contract.

## 5. Deployment inputs and ownership contract

| Input            | Owner / required proof                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Web/API hosts    | Release steward records real HTTPS hosts; Public Web, Management Web, and API are same-site under identity D2.                                                                                   |
| Cookies/CORS     | __Host- refresh cookie is Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax/Path=/ with no Domain; allowed exact Origins, credentialed cross-origin requests and refresh/logout are tested in both deployed Web apps. |
| Runtime scale    | One backend replica until shared rate-limit/security controls are separately approved and verified. Worker scheduling uses durable claims.                                                       |
| Secrets          | Backend-only database, merchant/signing, Storage, email, AI, push and credential-encryption inputs; client builds contain public API/project identifiers only.                                   |
| Database         | Migration steward records ordered forward migrations, latest compatible app version, restore point and disposable empty/upgrade verification.                                                    |
| Backup retention | Approved deployment requirement: rolling 30-day encrypted backups, restricted access, no forgotten indefinite exports; restore must replay approved erasure tombstones before reopening traffic. |
| Android          | Release owner records EAS project/profile/build ID, package/signing ownership, downloadable APK and install evidence; required target Android only.                                              |
| Evidence         | Module owner produces redacted requirement/race/real-provider evidence; steward composes release manifest without credentials/PII.                                                               |

The 30-day backup requirement is an approved explicit deployment default resolving the
identity-owned deferred backup purge input; actual host support is verified before go-live.
Restore cannot re-enable erased identity/guest data merely because backup is older.
Deployment vendor/host URLs and secrets are environment provisioning inputs, not a reason
to change auth transport or publish a Storage bucket without contract review.

Release manifest DTO contains `releaseId, createdAt, repositoryCommits[repo,sha],
apiContractSha256, migrationNames[], seedScenarioIds[], deploymentTargets[],
androidBuildId, evidenceLinks[], recoveryOwner, goNoGoResult`. No moving branch or
uncommitted schema is recorded as the release artifact. Every client lock points to the
exact backend digest in that manifest.

## 6. Deterministic seed and end-to-end scenario contract

Seeds use stable IDs/keys in the backend demo environment only and are idempotent.
They insert missing scenario data, verify existing matching immutable fixtures, and stop
on conflicting Manager-modified data rather than overwrite it. Provider-owned seed
adapters or approved command ports create each module's records; release does not
invent cross-module SQL mutations.

| Scenario                        | Required observation                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Restricted consultation         | One invitation/account/access; restricted Web timeline works; media/guest/seating/print denied.                                |
| Timeline/deposit                | Current mutual approval, stale revision rejected, verified sandbox/manual deposit confirms and promotes same identity.         |
| Private media/public invitation | Original private, approved derived asset public, one generic QR without household/RSVP/check-in scope.                         |
| Guests/headcount                | Default/custom stable groups, import/RSVP, higher then lower plan sequence; no headcount rollback.                             |
| Seating/print                   | Inclusive capacity, exception audit, invalidation blocks new print, exact printable/quote/charge snapshot, no recipient names. |
| Attendance                      | Duplicate names disambiguated, separate arrivals accumulate, over-expected succeeds, correction history preserved.             |
| Notifications                   | Real outbox, duplicate dedup, deadline revision/cancel behavior, credential-safe delivery, completion through booking port.    |
| Analytics                       | Known expected/actual, payments/refunds/credit, quotes excluded, historical hall/menu facts and source freshness.              |
| Cross-client                    | Couple Web/App and Manager/Staff Web use the same implemented API digest and backend denial semantics.                         |
| Recovery                        | Migration upgrade, health check, rollback-compatible deployment/restore drill with privacy controls.                           |

Use fake provider journeys in routine CI; final sandbox/staging journey explicitly records
which real services were used. Fake-only money/access/snapshot/provider checks never
satisfy integrated acceptance. EAS build/deployment occurs only in the actual release
workflow with user-approved environment/cost authority; this documentation does not
invoke or authorize paid cloud operations by itself.

## 7. Go/no-go and proposed parallel slices

No-go when any required module is unaccepted, migrations fail, API digests differ, the
deployed cookie/session flow fails, private data is public, an unresolved money intent is
treated as failed, or the Android artifact does not install. Monitor health/readiness,
outbox backlog, unknown payment/delivery outcomes, auth denial, and job failure using
bounded redacted metrics. The demo release has a named incident/recovery owner.

Rollback sequence: stop new money/print writes when required, restore last compatible
service/client artifacts, verify schema compatibility and outbox reconciliation, then
reopen writes. Never edit applied migrations or blindly replay payment callbacks/notification
intents. Database restoration requires controlled downtime, privacy tombstone replay and
dedup evidence reconciliation before reopening.

| Slice                                                  | Can overlap                                          | Hard prerequisite                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Deployment config validators/checklists/manifest tools | All module isolated implementation                   | Stable platform/auth contract.                                                 |
| Seed scenario adapters and CI fake journey             | Each source module becomes PROVIDER_READY            | No seed overwrite/direct cross-module repository bypass.                       |
| Staging migration and actual end-to-end seed           | Limited deployment checks may run per ready provider | Accepted migration sequence and real provider wiring.                          |
| Complete Android/demo release/go-live                  | Runs last                                            | Accepted 03–10, actual cookies/health/recovery, approved artifact/environment. |

Proposed waves: deployment/auth/config validation; deterministic seed/journey;
staging migration/monitoring; Android artifact/cross-client checks; recovery/evidence/
owner go-no-go (five). Independent scaffolding does not declare an unfinished provider
accepted. SPEC/plan approval order remains after approved 09/10 contracts; release
execution waits accepted implementations.

## 8. Verification record required at acceptance

Record command, immutable commit, environment label, UTC timestamp, pass/fail,
redacted output location, and responsible owner. Quality gates are the exact existing
scripts in the team/cross-repository guides; include browser runtime evidence for
deployed cookies/refresh/CORS and Android install/session restoration. A skipped check
is marked incomplete, with the dependent release step blocked.
```
